<Window x:Class="Engine.Windows.TradeWindow"
        xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
        xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
        xmlns:d="http://schemas.microsoft.com/expression/blend/2008"
        xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
        xmlns:local="clr-namespace:Engine.Windows"
        xmlns:viewModels="clr-namespace:Engine.ViewModels;assembly=Engine.ViewModels"
        d:DataContext="{d:DesignInstance viewModels:GameSession}"
        mc:Ignorable="d"
        FontSize="11pt"
        Title="Trade Screen" Height="480" Width="640">

    <Grid Margin ="10">
        <Grid.RowDefinitions>
            <RowDefinition Height ="Auto"/>
            <RowDefinition Height ="Auto"/>
            <RowDefinition Height ="*"/>
            <RowDefinition Height ="Auto"/>
        </Grid.RowDefinitions>    

        <Grid.ColumnDefinitions>
            <ColumnDefinition Width = "*"/>
            <ColumnDefinition Width = "*"/>
        </Grid.ColumnDefinitions>    

        <Label Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="0"
            Grid.ColumnSpan="2" HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Content="{Binding CurrentTrader.Name}"/>
        <Label Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="0"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Content="Your Inventory"/>
        <Label Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="1"
            HorizontalAlignment="Center"
            Content="Traders Inventory"/>
        <DataGrid Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="0" Margin = "10"
            ItemsSource="{Binding CurrentPlayer.Inventory.GroupedInventory}"
            AutoGenerateColumns="False"
            HeadersVisibility="Column"
            CanUserAddRows="False"
            CanUserDeleteRows="False"
            VerticalScrollBarVisibility="Auto">

            <DataGrid.Columns>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Description"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="*"
                                    Binding="{Binding Path=Item.Name}"/>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Qty"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="Auto"
                                    Binding="{Binding Quantity}"/>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Price"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="Auto"
                                    Binding="{Binding Path=Item.Price}"/>
                <DataGridTemplateColumn MinWidth="75">
                    <DataGridTemplateColumn.CellTemplate>
                        <DataTemplate>
                            <Button Click="OnClick_Sell"
                                    Width="55"
                                    Content="Sell 1"/>
                        </DataTemplate>
                    </DataGridTemplateColumn.CellTemplate>
                </DataGridTemplateColumn>
            </DataGrid.Columns>
 
        </DataGrid>
 
        <DataGrid Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="1"
                  Margin="10"
                  ItemsSource="{Binding CurrentTrader.Inventory.GroupedInventory}"
                  AutoGenerateColumns="False"
                  HeadersVisibility="Column"
                  CanUserAddRows="False"
                  CanUserDeleteRows="False"
                  VerticalScrollBarVisibility="Auto">
 
            <DataGrid.Columns>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Description"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="*"
                                    Binding="{Binding Path=Item.Name}"/>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Qty"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="Auto"
                                    Binding="{Binding Quantity}"/>
                <DataGridTextColumn Header="Price"
                                    IsReadOnly="True"
                                    Width="Auto"
                                    Binding="{Binding Path=Item.Price}"/>
                <DataGridTemplateColumn MinWidth="75">
                    <DataGridTemplateColumn.CellTemplate>
                        <DataTemplate>
                            <Button Click="OnClick_Buy"
                                    Width="55"
                                    Content="Buy"/>
                        </DataTemplate>
                    </DataGridTemplateColumn.CellTemplate>
                </DataGridTemplateColumn>
            </DataGrid.Columns>
 
        </DataGrid>
 
        <Button Grid.Row="3" Grid.Column="1"
                HorizontalAlignment="Right"
                Width="75"
                Content="Close"
                Click="OnClick_Close"/>
    </Grid>
</Window>

        <Button Grid.Row="2" Grid.Column="1"
                Content="Yes"
                Width="75"
                HorizontalAlignment="Right"

</Window>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1400" height="1250" viewBox="0 0 1400 1250" role="img" aria-labelledby="svgTitle svgDesc">
  <title id="svgTitle">RPG solution architecture</title>
  <desc id="svgDesc">Layered architecture of the WPF RPG: WPFUI, Engine.ViewModels, Engine.Services, Engine.Models and Engine.Core, with the game content files, save files, log files and the MSTest project alongside.</desc>
  <defs>
    <style>
      text { font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; }
      .title { font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; fill: #1f2328; }
      .sub   { font-size: 14px; fill: #57606a; }
      .band  { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; }
      .tag   { font-size: 12px; fill: #57606a; }
      .name  { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; fill: #1f2328; }
      .desc  { font-size: 11px; fill: #57606a; }
      .mono  { font-family: Consolas, 'Cascadia Mono', Menlo, monospace; font-size: 12px; fill: #1f2328; }
      .lbl   { font-size: 11.5px; fill: #3d444d; }
    </style>
    <marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#3d444d"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="ahr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#cc4b3c"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="ahg" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#8c959f"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- Opaque background so the diagram stays legible on dark themes -->
  <rect width="1400" height="1250" fill="#ffffff"/>

  <text class="title" x="40" y="50">RPG — solution architecture</text>

# Jakob's RPG A turn-based, tile-based role-playing game for Windows, written in **C# on .NET 9** with **WPF** and the **MVVM** pattern. You create a character, explore a small town, fight monsters, collect loot, finish quests, craft items and trade with shopkeepers. The game's content is loaded from XML/JSON files at startup: locations, monsters, items, quests, recipes, traders, races and attributes. You can add new content without touching the C# code.

--- ## Contents 1. [Features](#features) 2. [Getting started](#getting-started) 3. [How to play](#how-to-play) 4. [World map](#world-map) 5. [Game rules and formulas](#game-rules-and-formulas) 6. [Game content reference](#game-content-reference) 7. [Architecture](#architecture) 8. [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content) 9. [Save files](#save-files) 10. [Tests](#tests) 11. [Error handling and logging](#error-handling-and-logging) 12. [Known issues](#known-issues) 13. [Limitations and ideas](#limitations-and-ideas) 14. [Credits](#credits) --- ## Features | Area | What it does | |---|---| | **Character creation** | Choose a name and a race (Human, Elf, Orc). Six attributes are rolled with `3d6`, then race modifiers are applied. You can re-roll as often as you like. | | **Exploration** | A 9-location grid world. See [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content). | --- ## Getting started ### Requirements - **Windows 10 or 11**. WPF only runs on Windows, and the build's post-build step uses `xcopy`. - **.NET 9 SDK**. Built and tested with SDK `9.0.318`. - Optional: **Visual Studio 2022** (17.12 or later), or **VS Code** with the C# Dev Kit extension. ### Build, run and test From the repository root: ```powershell # Restore NuGet packages and build every project dotnet build rpg.sln # Start the game dotnet run --project WPFUI # Run the unit tests (22 tests, MSTest) dotnet test rpg.sln ``` In Visual Studio, open `rpg.sln`, set **WPFUI** as the startup project and press F5. > The build currently reports about 100 nullable-reference warnings (`CS86xx`) and no errors. They do not affect the game. ### How the game finds its data `WPFUI.csproj` and `Test/test.csproj` both have a post-build step that copies the whole `GameFiles/` folder into the build output: ```xml ``` After a build, the output folder (for example `WPFUI/bin/Debug/net9.0-windows/`) contains `GameData/*.xml`, `GameData/GameDetails.json` and `Images/**`. Every factory builds its path from `AppContext.BaseDirectory`, which is the folder containing the `.exe`, not the current working directory. That's why the game and the tests find their data no matter where they are started from. > **After editing anything in `GameFiles/`, rebuild** so the copy in `bin/` is refreshed. --- ## How to play ### Starting a game ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Startup Startup --> CharacterCreation: Start New Game Startup --> MainWindow: Load saved game (.rpg) Startup --> [*]: Exit CharacterCreation --> CharacterCreation: Roll new player CharacterCreation --> MainWindow: Use this player MainWindow --> TradeWindow: Trade button or T (modal) TradeWindow --> MainWindow: Close MainWindow --> SavePrompt: window closes (File → Exit, X button, File → New Game) SavePrompt --> [*]: Yes (save dialog) or No MainWindow --> Startup: File → New Game ``` 1. **Startup window.** Choose *Start New Game*, *Load saved game* or *Exit*. 2. **Character creation.** Type a name and pick a race. Game rules always use `ModifiedValue`. | Race | Modifiers | |---|---| | Human | CON +1 | | Elf | CHA +1, STR −1 | | Orc | STR +1, CHA −1 | > Only **Dexterity** affects gameplay at the moment, through initiative and hit chance. The other attributes are shown but not used yet. ### Experience and levels ``` Level = Experience / 100 + 1 (integer division) MaximumHitPoints = Level × 10 (set only when the level changes) ``` | Experience | Level | Max HP after reaching it | |---|---|---| | 0 – 99 | 1 | 10 (starting value) | | 100 – 199 | 2 | 20 | | 200 – 299 | 3 | 30 | | … | n | n × 10 | Levelling up raises your **maximum** HP but not your current HP. The message log shows *"You are now Level n"*. ### Combat 1. **Encounter.** When you enter a location that has monsters, one is picked at random. The `Percent` values in `Locations.xml` are **relative weights**, so they don't have to add up to 100. Each spawn is a fresh copy with its own weapon. Its loot is rolled at spawn time: each loot-table entry drops independently if `d100 ≤ Percentage`. 2. **Initiative.** A `Battle` starts immediately. If the monster wins initiative, **it attacks you the moment you arrive**. 3. **Your turn.** Each attack you make is resolved first. If the monster survives, it attacks back once. 4. **Hit check.** The same formula is used for initiative and for every attack: ``` dexOffset = (attackerDEX² − defenderDEX²) / 10 randomOffset = d20 − 10 // −9 … +10 success = d100 ≤ 50 + dexOffset + randomOffset ``` | Attacker DEX | Defender DEX | Chance to hit / go first | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | 10 | 10 | 41 % – 60 % | | 14 | 10 | 50 % – 69 % | | 18 | 3 | 72 % – 91 % | | 3 | 18 | 9 % – 28 % | 5. **Damage.** On a hit, the weapon's `DamageDice` are rolled (e.g. `1d2`). A creature at 0 HP or less is set to exactly 0 and dies. 6. **Victory.** You receive the monster's XP, gold and every item in its inventory. **A new monster of that location spawns immediately**, so fights chain until you leave. 7. **Fleeing.** Just walk away; the battle is thrown away. When you come back, a new monster is spawned. 8. **Consumables in combat.** Using a consumable does **not** give the monster a turn. ### Healing A healing item restores its `HitPointsToHeal`, capped at your maximum HP, and is then removed from your inventory. The only healing item is the **Granola bar** (+2 HP). ### Quests - **Receiving.** When you enter a location, you get every quest it offers that you don't already have. The message log lists the required items and the rewards. - **Completing.** Also when you enter that location. If you have all the required items, they are taken from you and you get the XP, gold and reward items. The quest is then marked *Done*. - The game checks for completions **before** it hands out new quests. So a quest can't be finished on the same visit you receive it. Step out and come back in. ### Crafting *Craft* checks that you have every ingredient in the required quantity. If you do, the ingredients are removed and the output items are added. If not, the message log lists what's needed. New recipes can only be learned in code for now; see [Limitations](#limitations-and-ideas). ### Trading - *Buy* and *Sell 1* use the item's `Price` in both directions, with no markup. - Each trader starts with **9999 gold** and will refuse a sale they can't afford. - If you sell your equipped weapon or consumable, it is unequipped. - Trader stock and gold live in memory for as long as the app runs. They are shared across new games in the same session and are **not** saved. ### Death and respawn When your HP reaches 0 the log shows *"You have been killed"*. You are moved to **Home (0, −1)** and healed to full. You keep your inventory, gold, XP and quests. --- ## Game content reference ### Items — [`GameItems.xml`](GameFiles/GameData/GameItems.xml) | ID | Name | Category | Price | Effect / use | |---:|---|---|---:|---| | 1001 | Pointy stick | Weapon | 1 | `1d2` damage · starting weapon, sold by every trader | | 1002 | Rusty sword | Weapon | 5 | `1d3` damage · quest reward | | 1501 | Snake fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Snake's natural weapon | | 1502 | Rat claw | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Rat's natural weapon | | 1503 | Spider fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d4` · the Giant Spider's natural weapon | | 2001 | Granola bar | Consumable | 5 | Heals 2 HP · craftable | | 3001 | Oats | Miscellaneous | 1 | Crafting ingredient | | 3002 | Honey | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 3003 | Raisins | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 9001 | Snake fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Snake loot · **quest item** | | 9002 | Snakeskin | Miscellaneous | 2 | Snake loot | | 9003 | Rat tail | Miscellaneous | 1 | Rat loot | | 9004 | Rat fur | Miscellaneous | 2 | Rat loot | | 9005 | Spider fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Spider loot | | 9006 | Spider silk | Miscellaneous | 2 | Spider loot | The 15xx "natural weapons" and the 9xxx loot items can share a name. ### Layers in detail **Engine.Core** holds infrastructure with no game rules: - [`DiceService`](Engine.Core/DiceService.cs) is a singleton (`DiceService.Instance`) over the D20Tek library. It accepts dice notation (`Roll("3d6")`) or sides/count/modifier (`Roll(100)`). `Configure(RollerType.Constant, constantValue: n)` swaps in a fixed roller, which is useful for deterministic tests. - [`MessageBroker`](Engine.Core/MessageBroker.cs) is a singleton (`MessageBroker.GetInstance()`). Game code calls `RaiseMessage(text)`, and the UI listens to `OnMessageRaised`. This keeps the game logic from ever referencing a WPF control. - [`LoggingService`](Engine.Core/LoggingService.cs) is static. It writes an exception, and recursively its inner exceptions, to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`. **Engine.Models** holds the domain: - [`LivingEntity`](Engine.Models/LivingEntity.cs) is the abstract base for anything with HP, gold, a level, attributes and an inventory. It exposes `TakeDamage`, `Heal`, `CompleteHeal`, `ReceiveGold`, `SpendGold`, `AddItemToInventory`, `RemoveItemFromInventory`, `UseCurrentWeaponOn(target)` and `UseCurrentConsumable()`. It raises `OnKilled` and relays its equipped item's action text as `OnActionPerformed`. - [`Player`](Engine.Models/Player.cs) adds `Experience`, `CharacterClass`, `Quests`, `Recipes`, `AddExperience` (with level-up) and `LearnRecipe`. - [`Monster`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs) adds `ID`, `ImageName`, `RewardedExperiencePoints` and a `LootTable`. `Clone()` gives every spawn its own weapon. - [`Trader`](Engine.Models/Trader.cs) is a `LivingEntity` with 9999 HP and gold and no attributes. - [`GameItem`](Engine.Models/GameItem.cs) has a `Category` (Weapon, Consumable, Miscellanous), an `ItemTypeId`, `Name`, `Price`, `IsUnique` and an optional `IAction`. Its `Clone()` also clones the action and binds it to the new item. - [`IAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/IAction.cs) has two implementations. [`AttackWithWeapon`](Engine.Models/Actions/AttackWithWeapon.cs) does a hit roll, then rolls damage dice. [`Heal`](Engine.Models/Actions/Heal.cs) restores HP. Both inherit [`BaseAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/BaseActions.cs), which raises `OnActionPerformed` with a human-readable result. - [`Inventory`](Engine.Models/Inventory.cs) is immutable. `AddItem(s)` and `RemoveItem(s)` return a **new** `Inventory`. It exposes `Items`, `GroupedInventory` (for the grids), `Weapons`, `Consumables`, `HasConsumable` and `HasAllTheseItems(...)`. - [`Battle`](Engine.Models/Battle.cs) owns one fight. It subscribes to both combatants' events, rolls initiative, runs the attack → counter-attack exchange, hands out rewards and raises `OnCombatVictory`. It is `IDisposable` so it can unhook its event handlers. - [`World`](Engine.Models/World.cs) and [`Location`](Engine.Models/Location.cs) form the grid. `LocationAt(x, y)` finds a location. Each location has a name, description, image, `MonstersHere` (weighted), `QuestsAvailableHere` and `TraderHere`. - [`Quest`](Engine.Models/Quest.cs) / [`QuestStatus`](Engine.Models/QuestStatus.cs) / [`Recipe`](Engine.Models/Recipe.cs) are built from [`ItemQuantity`](Engine.Models/ItemQuantity.cs) lists. They also build the tooltip text shown in the UI. - [`GameDetails`](Engine.Models/GameDetails.cs), [`Race`](Engine.Models/Race.cs), [`PlayerAttribute`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttribute.cs) and [`PlayerAttributeModifier`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttributeModifier.cs) are the ruleset loaded from `GameDetails.json`. - [`GameState`](Engine.Models/GameState.cs) is what gets saved: the `Player` plus the x/y coordinates. **Engine.Services** turns data files into model objects: - Each factory is a **static class** whose **static constructor** reads its XML file once and keeps "prototype" objects. The public methods return **clones**, so no two holders share state. - [`GameDetailService`](Engine.Services/GameDetailService.cs) parses `GameDetails.json` with Newtonsoft `JObject`. - [`SaveGameService`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs) serialises a `GameState` to JSON. On load, it rebuilds the `Player` and resolves items, quests and recipes **by ID** through the factories. **Engine.ViewModels** holds the state the UI binds to: - [`GameSession`](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs) is the running game. The heart of the game loop is the `CurrentLocation` setter; see the flowchart below. It exposes `MoveNorth/East/South/West`, `AttackCurrentMonster`, `UseCurrentConsumable` and `CraftItemUsing(recipe)`, plus `HasLocationToNorth/…`, `HasMonster` and `HasTrader` for button visibility. - [`CharacterCreationViewModel`](Engine.ViewModels/CharacterCreationViewModel.cs) rolls attributes, applies race modifiers, and builds the starting `Player` with its starter kit. **WPFUI** holds the views: - Windows are thin. Code-behind forwards button clicks and key presses to `GameSession` methods, and bindings display the state. - [`FileToBitmapConverter`](WPFUI/CustomConverters/FileToBitmapConverter.cs) turns an image path like `./Images/Monsters/Snake.png` into a cached `BitmapImage`, resolved against the `.exe` folder. ### Design patterns | Pattern | Where | Why | |---|---|---| | **MVVM** | `GameSession` / `CharacterCreationViewModel` are the windows' `DataContext` | The UI has no game logic, and the view models can be unit-tested without WPF. | | **Weaved `INotifyPropertyChanged`** | `FodyWeavers.xml` in Models and ViewModels (``) | Classes only declare `event PropertyChanged`. Fody injects the notify calls into every setter at compile time, including for computed properties that depend on them (`IsAlive`, `HasMonster`, `HasLocationToNorth`…). `[DoNotCheckEquality]` on `CurrentLocation` makes the setter run even when you "move" to the same location, for example respawning at Home while already there. | | **Factory + Prototype** | `ItemFactory`, `MonsterFactory`, … | Data is parsed once. Each request gets a `Clone()`, so two Snakes (or two Pointy sticks) never share HP, weapons or event subscribers. | | **Singleton** | `DiceService.Instance`, `MessageBroker.GetInstance()` | One random source and one message channel for the whole game. | | **Observer / events** | See the event table below | Loose coupling between actions, entities, battles, the session and the UI. | | **Strategy (pluggable behaviour)** | `GameItem.Action : IAction` | New item behaviours need no changes to `LivingEntity` or `Battle`. | | **Immutable object** | `Inventory` | Every change creates a new `Inventory` and assigns it to `LivingEntity.Inventory`. That single `PropertyChanged` refreshes every bound list: grids, weapon box, consumable box. | | **Disposable subscription** | `Battle : IDisposable` | When a monster is replaced, its old battle unhooks its handlers, so dead fights can't post messages. | | **Data-driven content** | `GameFiles/GameData` | Designers can add content without recompiling the engine; a rebuild just copies the As a result, a missing or malformed file surfaces as a `TypeInitializationException` wrapping the real `FileNotFoundException` or `ArgumentException`, the first time that factory is touched. ### Events and messages | Event | Declared in | Raised when | Handled by | |---|---|---|---| | `MessageBroker.OnMessageRaised` | Engine.Core | Anything calls `RaiseMessage(text)` | `MainWindow` appends a paragraph to the message log and scrolls to the end | | `IAction.OnActionPerformed` | `BaseAction` | An action finishes (`"X hit Y for 2 points"`) | The `LivingEntity` that has that item equipped | | `LivingEntity.OnActionPerformed` | `LivingEntity` | Relays its equipped item's action text | `Battle` (for both combatants). `GameSession` subscribes briefly when a consumable is used outside combat. | | `LivingEntity.OnKilled` | `LivingEntity` | HP drops to 0 | `Battle` (monster died → rewards). `GameSession` (player died → respawn). | | `Player.OnLeveledUp` | `Player` | `AddExperience` changes the level | `GameSession` → *"You are now Level n"* | | `Battle.OnCombatVictory` | `Battle` | After rewards are handed out | `GameSession` → spawns the next monster | | `PropertyChanged` | Every model/view-model class (woven by Fody) | Any property setter | WPF data bindings | ### Why items and monsters are cloned A `GameItem`'s `IAction` raises `OnActionPerformed`, and the entity holding the item subscribes to it. If two monsters shared one weapon object, one monster's attack would be reported through the other monster's handlers as well. To avoid this: - `GameItem.Clone()` creates a new item **and** calls `Action.Clone(newItem)`, so every item instance has its own action and its own subscribers. - `Monster.Clone()` clones its weapon for every spawn. - The regression test `TestCombat.TwoHoldersOfTheSameItemTypeDoNotShareActionMessages` guards this. --- ## Adding or changing content All content lives in [`GameFiles/GameData`](GameFiles/GameData). After editing, **rebuild** so the files are copied next to the `.exe`. General rules: - **IDs must match across files.** A monster's `WeaponID`, a loot `ID`, a quest item, a recipe ingredient or a trader's stock must all exist in `GameItems.xml`. A missing ID fails at load time with `ArgumentException: ItemTypeId 'n' does not exist`. - **Element and attribute names are case-sensitive.** The factories use XPath such as `/GameItems/Weapons/Weapon`. - **Images** go in `GameFiles/Images/Locations` or `GameFiles/Images/Monsters` and are referenced by file name only. The UI draws them in a 125 × 125 box. - Every entity that fights needs a **`DEX`** attribute, because `Battle` and `AttackWithWeapon` call `GetAttribute("DEX")`. ### `GameDetails.json`: attributes and races ```json { "Name": "RPG", "Version": "0.1.000", "PlayerAttributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6" } ], "Races": [ { "Key": "ELF", "DisplayName": "Elf", "PlayerAttributeModifiers": [ { "Key": "CHA", "Modifier": "1" }, { "Key": "STR", "Modifier": "-1" } ] } ] } ``` | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `PlayerAttributes[].Key` | Short key used by code and modifiers (`DEX` is required for combat) | | `PlayerAttributes[].DiceNotation` | Any D20Tek notation, e.g. `3d6`, `4d6k3`, `2d8+2` | | `Races[]` | Optional. If there are none, the race picker is hidden. | | `PlayerAttributeModifiers[].Modifier` | Added to the rolled value to give `ModifiedValue` | ### `GameItems.xml`: items ```xml ``` | Element | Category | Extra attributes | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `Weapon` | Weapon | `DamageDice` (dice notation, required) | Gets an `AttackWithWeapon` action. Unique: shown one per row. | | `HealingItem` | Consumable | `HitPointsToHeal` (int) | Gets a `Heal` action. Used up when used. | | `MiscellaneousItem` | Miscellanous | — | Loot, quest items, crafting ingredients. | The ID ranges used so far are a convention, not a rule: 1xxx player weapons, 15xx monster weapons, 2xxx healing, 3xxx ingredients, 9xxx monster loot. ### `Monsters.xml`: monsters ```xml 15 ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `WeaponID` | Must be a **`Weapon`** item. Its `DamageDice` is the monster's damage. | | `RewardXP`, `Gold` | Given to the player when the monster dies | | `` | The monster's DEX (see [Known issues](#known-issues)) | | `LootItem Percentage` | Independent drop chance, 0–100, rolled when the monster spawns | ### `Locations.xml`: the world ```xml ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `X`, `Y` | Grid position. Must be unique. Neighbours are connected automatically. | | `Monsters/Monster Percent` | Relative spawn weight. With `Rat=75, Snake=25`, rats appear 3× as often. | | `Quests/Quest ID` | Quest offered **and** turned in here | | `Trader ID` | At most one trader per location | ### `Quests.xml`, `Recipes.xml` and `Traders.xml` ```xml ``` > `QuestFactory` silently loads nothing if `Quests.xml` is missing. Every other factory throws `FileNotFoundException`. ### Example: add a wolf and a new location 1. **`GameItems.xml`**: add a natural weapon and a loot item: ```xml ``` 2. **`Monsters.xml`**: add the monster: ```xml 13 ``` 3. **`Locations.xml`**: place it east of the Spider Forest, so the forest gets an *East* button automatically: ```xml ``` 4. Add `GameFiles/Images/Monsters/Wolf.png` and `GameFiles/Images/Locations/DarkWoods.png`. 5. Rebuild and run. --- ## Save files - **Saving.** Use *File → Save Game*, or answer *Yes* when closing the main window. A save dialog opens in the `.exe` folder with the filter `*.rpg`. - **Loading.** Use *Load saved game* on the Startup window. - **Format.** `SaveGameService` writes an indented JSON copy of `GameState`. Properties marked `[JsonIgnore]` are left out, so items, quests and recipes are stored **by ID only** and rebuilt from the factories on load. Example (abridged): ```json { "Player": { "CharacterClass": "Fighter", "Experience": 35, "Quests": [ { "Quest": { "Id": 1 }, "IsCompleted": false } ], "Recipes": [ { "ID": 1 } ], "Attributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 11, "ModifiedValue": 12 }, { "Key": "DEX", "DisplayName": "Dexterity", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 14, "ModifiedValue": 14 } ], "Name": "Jakob", "CurrentHitPoints": 8, "MaximumHitPoints": 10, "Gold": 17, "Level": 1, "Inventory": { "Items": [ { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 2001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 9001 } ] }, "CurrentWeapon": { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, "CurrentConsumable": null }, "XCoordinate": 0, "YCoordinate": 2 } ``` | Data | Saved | Restored on load | |---|:---:|:---:| | Name, class, XP (level is recalculated), max / current HP, gold | ✔ | ✔ | | Attributes (base and modified values; the race is already applied) | ✔ | ✔ | | Inventory (by `ItemTypeId`) | ✔ | ✔ | | Quests (ID + completed flag), known recipes (ID) | ✔ | ✔ | | Position (x, y) | ✔ | ✔ | | Equipped weapon / consumable | ✔ | ✘ (choose it again after loading) | | Trader stock and gold, the current monster | ✘ | ✘ (a new monster spawns on arrival) | A missing file throws `FileNotFoundException`. Any problem while reading the JSON is reported as `FormatException: Error reading: `. --- ## Tests ```powershell dotnet test rpg.sln # everything dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TestInventory" # one class dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "Name=EnoughAttacksKillsAMonster" # one test ``` The suite has 22 MSTest tests, and all pass. The test project's post-build step copies `GameFiles/` into its output folder, so the factories load the real game data. | Class (file) | Tests | What is covered | |---|:---:|---| | `TestAttackWithWeapon` ([Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs](Test/Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs)) | 3 | Valid construction. Throws `ArgumentException` for a non-weapon item or empty dice notation. | | `TestCombat` ([Models/TestCombat.cs](Test/Models/TestCombat.cs)) | 4 | Attacks reduce HP. Enough attacks kill (HP ends at exactly 0 and `OnKilled` fires). Consumables heal, are used up and are unequipped. Two monsters with the same weapon type don't share action messages. | | `TestInventory` ([Models/TestInventory.cs](Test/Models/TestInventory.cs)) | 9 | Empty inventory, add/remove single and multiple items, category views (`Weapons`, `Consumables`), removing by `ItemQuantity`, and removing more than you have (throws `InvalidOperationException`). | | `TestPlayer` ([Models/TestPlayer.cs](Test/Models/TestPlayer.cs)) | 4 | The constructor keeps the max HP it's given and doesn't raise `OnLeveledUp`. Level-up at 100 XP (max HP 20, event raised once). Selling the equipped weapon unequips it. | | `TestGameSession` ([ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs](Test/ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs)) | 2 | A new session starts at Home. Dying moves the player back Home fully healed. | Test helpers: - [`TestPlayerBuilder`](Test/TestPlayerBuilder.cs) creates players with **fixed** attribute values, so tests don't depend on dice rolls. `TestCombat` gives the player DEX 30, which pushes the hit chance above 100 %. - [`TestInventoryExtensions`](Test/TestInventoryExtensions.cs) adds factory-backed helpers (`AddItemFromFactory`, `AddItems(ItemQuantity…)`) that only the tests need, so `Inventory` itself stays independent of `ItemFactory`. --- ## Error handling and logging | Where | What happens | |---|---| | Factories | Missing data file → `FileNotFoundException`. Unknown ID → `ArgumentException`. Both are wrapped in `TypeInitializationException` when thrown from a static constructor. | | `AttackWithWeapon` / `Heal` constructors | `ArgumentException` if the item has the wrong category or the dice notation is empty | | `LivingEntity.SpendGold` | `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when spending more than you have. The trade window checks this first. | | `SaveGameService` | `FileNotFoundException` / `FormatException` | | `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` ([App.xaml.cs](WPFUI/App.xaml.cs)) | Logs the exception with `LoggingService` and shows a message box. **Note:** not wired up yet, see below. | | `LoggingService` | Appends to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`: timestamp, message, stack trace, then the same for every inner exception. | Log entry format: ``` EXCEPTION: 29.09.2026 14:03:12 ======================================== Object reference not set to an instance of an object. at Engine.ViewModels.GameSession.set_CurrentMonster(Monster value) ... INNER EXCEPTION ---------------------------------------- ... ``` --- ## Known issues I found these by reading the code. They are listed roughly by impact, each with a suggested fix. 1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity.** [`MonsterFactory.LoadMonstersFromNodes`](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs#L69-L78) writes each monster's `` into the **same** shared `PlayerAttribute` objects and passes them to every `Monster`. [`Monster.Clone`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs#L29) then shares them again. As a result, all monsters end up with the last value loaded, the Giant Spider's 12. *Fix:* create new `PlayerAttribute` instances per monster, and copy them in `Clone()`. 2. **Possible crash when a monster kills you the moment you arrive.** If a monster wins initiative, it attacks inside the `Battle` constructor. If that attack kills the player, `OnPlayerKilled` moves them Home. That sets `CurrentMonster = null` while `_currentBattle` is still `null`, and [the setter](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs#L66-L71) dereferences it, which throws a `NullReferenceException`. The easiest way to hit this is to walk into the Spider Forest with 1–2 HP. *Fix:* start the first attack after `GameSession` has stored the battle (e.g. a separate `Battle.Start()`), and null-check `_currentBattle`. 3. **The unhandled-exception logger is never called.** `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` exists, but [`App.xaml`](WPFUI/App.xaml#L1-L6) doesn't hook it up. As a result, errors crash the app and nothing is written to `Logs/`. *Fix:* add `DispatcherUnhandledException="App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException"` to the `` element. 4. **The consumable controls are always visible.** [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L249) binds to `Inventory.HasConsumables`, but the property is called `HasConsumable`. The binding fails, so the visibility falls back to *Visible*. 5. **Overlapping rows in the player panel.** In [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L55-L85), *Experience* (row 5), *Gold* (row 6, which is clamped to row 5 because the grid has only 6 rows) and the attribute list (row 5) share one grid row and are drawn on top of each other. 6. **The Startup window has no title.** [`Startup.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/Startup.xaml#L11) binds `Title` to `GameDetails.Title`, which doesn't exist. `GameDetails.Name` was probably meant. 7. **The equipped weapon isn't restored after loading.** It is saved, but [`SaveGameService.CreatePlayer`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs#L39-L55) never reads it back. Select a weapon again after loading. 8. **T opens the trade screen even where there is no trader.** The result is an empty trade window. The hotkey should check `HasTrader` first ([MainWindow.xaml.cs](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L90)). 9. **A stale test file.** [`Test/Services/TestCombatServices`](Test/Services/TestCombatServices) has no `.cs` extension and refers to a `CombatService` class that no longer exists, so it isn't compiled. Delete it, or port it to `Battle`. 10. **`RPGState.json` is a save file from an older version.** It uses `CurrentPlayer` / `CurrentLocation` keys and cannot be loaded by the current `SaveGameService`, which expects `Player` / `XCoordinate` / `YCoordinate` in a `.rpg` file. 11. **Content typo.** The Farmer's House description mentions "Farmer **Fred**", but the trader there is "Farmer **Ted**". --- ## Limitations and ideas - Only **DEX** is used by the rules. STR could scale damage, CON could raise max HP, and CHA could affect trade prices. - **Recipes can only be learned in code** (`CharacterCreationViewModel.GetPlayer`). A recipe reward on quests or a recipe trader would open up crafting. - All three traders only stock a Pointy stick, so **crafting ingredients can't be bought** once the starting ones are used. - There is **no armour** and no defence value. Hit chance depends only on DEX. - **Levelling up doesn't heal**, and `CharacterClass` is always `"Fighter"`. - The *Help* and *About* menu items are placeholders (disabled). - **Traders aren't saved**, and they keep their state across new games in the same app session. - Windows-only: WPF plus the `xcopy` post-build step. --- ## Credits - The game's structure and starter content follow **Scott Lilly's "Build a C#/WPF RPG" tutorial series (SOSCSRPG)**. The commit history tracks progress through its lessons. - Libraries used: - [D20Tek.DiceNotation](https://github.com/d20Tek/DiceNotation) for dice rolling. - [Fody](https://github.com/Fody/Fody) / [PropertyChanged.Fody](https://github.com/Fody/PropertyChanged) for automatic `INotifyPropertyChanged`. - [Newtonsoft.Json](https://www.newtonsoft.com/json) for JSON. - [MSTest](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx) for tests.

# Jakob's RPG A turn-based, tile-based role-playing game for Windows, written in **C# on .NET 9** with **WPF** and the **MVVM** pattern. You create a character, explore a small town, fight monsters, collect loot, finish quests, craft items and trade with shopkeepers. The game's content is loaded from XML/JSON files at startup: locations, monsters, items, quests, recipes, traders, races and attributes. You can add new content without touching the C# code.

--- ## Contents 1. [Features](#features) 2. [Getting started](#getting-started) 3. [How to play](#how-to-play) 4. [World map](#world-map) 5. [Game rules and formulas](#game-rules-and-formulas) 6. [Game content reference](#game-content-reference) 7. [Architecture](#architecture) 8. [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content) 9. [Save files](#save-files) 10. [Tests](#tests) 11. [Error handling and logging](#error-handling-and-logging) 12. [Known issues](#known-issues) 13. [Limitations and ideas](#limitations-and-ideas) 14. [Credits](#credits) --- ## Features | Area | What it does | |---|---| | **Character creation** | Choose a name and a race (Human, Elf, Orc). Six attributes are rolled with `3d6`, then race modifiers are applied. You can re-roll as often as you like. | | **Exploration** | A 9-location grid world. You move north, east, south or west with buttons or the `W` `A` `S` `D` keys. A direction button only appears when a location exists in that direction. | | **Combat** | Turn-based. Initiative and hit chance come from Dexterity plus a random roll, and damage comes from the weapon's dice notation (e.g. `1d4`). | | **Loot and progression** | Monsters drop gold, experience and items from a per-monster loot table. Every 100 XP gives you a level and raises your maximum HP. | | **Quests** | You receive a quest automatically when you enter the location that offers it. You complete it automatically when you come back with the required items. | | **Crafting** | Turn ingredients into items with recipes you know (e.g. Oats + Honey + Raisins → Granola bar). | | **Trading** | Buy and sell items with three traders at the item's listed price. | | **Consumables** | Healing items restore hit points and are used up. | | **Save / load** | Save to a `.rpg` file (JSON) and load it again from the start screen. You are asked whether to save every time the game window closes. | | **Death** | When you die you wake up at Home with full health. You keep your items, gold and XP. | | **Data-driven** | All content lives in [`GameFiles/GameData`](GameFiles/GameData). See [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content). | --- ## Getting started ### Requirements - **Windows 10 or 11**. WPF only runs on Windows, and the build's post-build step uses `xcopy`. - **.NET 9 SDK**. Built and tested with SDK `9.0.318`. - Optional: **Visual Studio 2022** (17.12 or later), or **VS Code** with the C# Dev Kit extension. ### Build, run and test From the repository root: ```powershell # Restore NuGet packages and build every project dotnet build rpg.sln # Start the game dotnet run --project WPFUI # Run the unit tests (22 tests, MSTest) dotnet test rpg.sln ``` In Visual Studio, open `rpg.sln`, set **WPFUI** as the startup project and press F5. > The build currently reports about 100 nullable-reference warnings (`CS86xx`) and no errors. They do not affect the game. ### How the game finds its data `WPFUI.csproj` and `Test/test.csproj` both have a post-build step that copies the whole `GameFiles/` folder into the build output: ```xml ``` After a build, the output folder (for example `WPFUI/bin/Debug/net9.0-windows/`) contains `GameData/*.xml`, `GameData/GameDetails.json` and `Images/**`. Every factory builds its path from `AppContext.BaseDirectory`, which is the folder containing the `.exe`, not the current working directory. That's why the game and the tests find their data no matter where they are started from. > **After editing anything in `GameFiles/`, rebuild** so the copy in `bin/` is refreshed. --- ## How to play ### Starting a game ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Startup Startup --> CharacterCreation: Start New Game Startup --> MainWindow: Load saved game (.rpg) Startup --> [*]: Exit CharacterCreation --> CharacterCreation: Roll new player CharacterCreation --> MainWindow: Use this player MainWindow --> TradeWindow: Trade button or T (modal) TradeWindow --> MainWindow: Close MainWindow --> SavePrompt: window closes (File → Exit, X button, File → New Game) SavePrompt --> [*]: Yes (save dialog) or No MainWindow --> Startup: File → New Game ``` 1. **Startup window.** Choose *Start New Game*, *Load saved game* or *Exit*. 2. **Character creation.** Type a name and pick a race. Game rules always use `ModifiedValue`. | Race | Modifiers | |---|---| | Human | CON +1 | | Elf | CHA +1, STR −1 | | Orc | STR +1, CHA −1 | > Only **Dexterity** affects gameplay at the moment, through initiative and hit chance. The other attributes are shown but not used yet. ### Experience and levels ``` Level = Experience / 100 + 1 (integer division) MaximumHitPoints = Level × 10 (set only when the level changes) ``` | Experience | Level | Max HP after reaching it | |---|---|---| | 0 – 99 | 1 | 10 (starting value) | | 100 – 199 | 2 | 20 | | 200 – 299 | 3 | 30 | | … | n | n × 10 | Levelling up raises your **maximum** HP but not your current HP. The message log shows *"You are now Level n"*. ### Combat 1. **Encounter.** When you enter a location that has monsters, one is picked at random. The `Percent` values in `Locations.xml` are **relative weights**, so they don't have to add up to 100. Each spawn is a fresh copy with its own weapon. Its loot is rolled at spawn time: each loot-table entry drops independently if `d100 ≤ Percentage`. 2. **Initiative.** A `Battle` starts immediately. If the monster wins initiative, **it attacks you the moment you arrive**. 3. **Your turn.** Each attack you make is resolved first. If the monster survives, it attacks back once. 4. **Hit check.** The same formula is used for initiative and for every attack: ``` dexOffset = (attackerDEX² − defenderDEX²) / 10 randomOffset = d20 − 10 // −9 … +10 success = d100 ≤ 50 + dexOffset + randomOffset ``` | Attacker DEX | Defender DEX | Chance to hit / go first | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | 10 | 10 | 41 % – 60 % | | 14 | 10 | 50 % – 69 % | | 18 | 3 | 72 % – 91 % | | 3 | 18 | 9 % – 28 % | 5. **Damage.** On a hit, the weapon's `DamageDice` are rolled (e.g. `1d2`). A creature at 0 HP or less is set to exactly 0 and dies. 6. **Victory.** You receive the monster's XP, gold and every item in its inventory. **A new monster of that location spawns immediately**, so fights chain until you leave. 7. **Fleeing.** Just walk away; the battle is thrown away. When you come back, a new monster is spawned. 8. **Consumables in combat.** Using a consumable does **not** give the monster a turn. ### Healing A healing item restores its `HitPointsToHeal`, capped at your maximum HP, and is then removed from your inventory. The only healing item is the **Granola bar** (+2 HP). ### Quests - **Receiving.** When you enter a location, you get every quest it offers that you don't already have. The message log lists the required items and the rewards. - **Completing.** Also when you enter that location. If you have all the required items, they are taken from you and you get the XP, gold and reward items. The quest is then marked *Done*. - The game checks for completions **before** it hands out new quests. So a quest can't be finished on the same visit you receive it. Step out and come back in. ### Crafting *Craft* checks that you have every ingredient in the required quantity. If you do, the ingredients are removed and the output items are added. If not, the message log lists what's needed. New recipes can only be learned in code for now; see [Limitations](#limitations-and-ideas). ### Trading - *Buy* and *Sell 1* use the item's `Price` in both directions, with no markup. - Each trader starts with **9999 gold** and will refuse a sale they can't afford. - If you sell your equipped weapon or consumable, it is unequipped. - Trader stock and gold live in memory for as long as the app runs. They are shared across new games in the same session and are **not** saved. ### Death and respawn When your HP reaches 0 the log shows *"You have been killed"*. You are moved to **Home (0, −1)** and healed to full. You keep your inventory, gold, XP and quests. --- ## Game content reference ### Items — [`GameItems.xml`](GameFiles/GameData/GameItems.xml) | ID | Name | Category | Price | Effect / use | |---:|---|---|---:|---| | 1001 | Pointy stick | Weapon | 1 | `1d2` damage · starting weapon, sold by every trader | | 1002 | Rusty sword | Weapon | 5 | `1d3` damage · quest reward | | 1501 | Snake fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Snake's natural weapon | | 1502 | Rat claw | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Rat's natural weapon | | 1503 | Spider fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d4` · the Giant Spider's natural weapon | | 2001 | Granola bar | Consumable | 5 | Heals 2 HP · craftable | | 3001 | Oats | Miscellaneous | 1 | Crafting ingredient | | 3002 | Honey | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 3003 | Raisins | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 9001 | Snake fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Snake loot · **quest item** | | 9002 | Snakeskin | Miscellaneous | 2 | Snake loot | | 9003 | Rat tail | Miscellaneous | 1 | Rat loot | | 9004 | Rat fur | Miscellaneous | 2 | Rat loot | | 9005 | Spider fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Spider loot | | 9006 | Spider silk | Miscellaneous | 2 | Spider loot | The 15xx "natural weapons" and the 9xxx loot items can share a name. ### Layers in detail **Engine.Core** holds infrastructure with no game rules: - [`DiceService`](Engine.Core/DiceService.cs) is a singleton (`DiceService.Instance`) over the D20Tek library. It accepts dice notation (`Roll("3d6")`) or sides/count/modifier (`Roll(100)`). `Configure(RollerType.Constant, constantValue: n)` swaps in a fixed roller, which is useful for deterministic tests. - [`MessageBroker`](Engine.Core/MessageBroker.cs) is a singleton (`MessageBroker.GetInstance()`). Game code calls `RaiseMessage(text)`, and the UI listens to `OnMessageRaised`. This keeps the game logic from ever referencing a WPF control. - [`LoggingService`](Engine.Core/LoggingService.cs) is static. It writes an exception, and recursively its inner exceptions, to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`. **Engine.Models** holds the domain: - [`LivingEntity`](Engine.Models/LivingEntity.cs) is the abstract base for anything with HP, gold, a level, attributes and an inventory. It exposes `TakeDamage`, `Heal`, `CompleteHeal`, `ReceiveGold`, `SpendGold`, `AddItemToInventory`, `RemoveItemFromInventory`, `UseCurrentWeaponOn(target)` and `UseCurrentConsumable()`. It raises `OnKilled` and relays its equipped item's action text as `OnActionPerformed`. - [`Player`](Engine.Models/Player.cs) adds `Experience`, `CharacterClass`, `Quests`, `Recipes`, `AddExperience` (with level-up) and `LearnRecipe`. - [`Monster`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs) adds `ID`, `ImageName`, `RewardedExperiencePoints` and a `LootTable`. `Clone()` gives every spawn its own weapon. - [`Trader`](Engine.Models/Trader.cs) is a `LivingEntity` with 9999 HP and gold and no attributes. - [`GameItem`](Engine.Models/GameItem.cs) has a `Category` (Weapon, Consumable, Miscellanous), an `ItemTypeId`, `Name`, `Price`, `IsUnique` and an optional `IAction`. Its `Clone()` also clones the action and binds it to the new item. - [`IAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/IAction.cs) has two implementations. [`AttackWithWeapon`](Engine.Models/Actions/AttackWithWeapon.cs) does a hit roll, then rolls damage dice. [`Heal`](Engine.Models/Actions/Heal.cs) restores HP. Both inherit [`BaseAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/BaseActions.cs), which raises `OnActionPerformed` with a human-readable result. - [`Inventory`](Engine.Models/Inventory.cs) is immutable. `AddItem(s)` and `RemoveItem(s)` return a **new** `Inventory`. It exposes `Items`, `GroupedInventory` (for the grids), `Weapons`, `Consumables`, `HasConsumable` and `HasAllTheseItems(...)`. - [`Battle`](Engine.Models/Battle.cs) owns one fight. It subscribes to both combatants' events, rolls initiative, runs the attack → counter-attack exchange, hands out rewards and raises `OnCombatVictory`. It is `IDisposable` so it can unhook its event handlers. - [`World`](Engine.Models/World.cs) and [`Location`](Engine.Models/Location.cs) form the grid. `LocationAt(x, y)` finds a location. Each location has a name, description, image, `MonstersHere` (weighted), `QuestsAvailableHere` and `TraderHere`. - [`Quest`](Engine.Models/Quest.cs) / [`QuestStatus`](Engine.Models/QuestStatus.cs) / [`Recipe`](Engine.Models/Recipe.cs) are built from [`ItemQuantity`](Engine.Models/ItemQuantity.cs) lists. They also build the tooltip text shown in the UI. - [`GameDetails`](Engine.Models/GameDetails.cs), [`Race`](Engine.Models/Race.cs), [`PlayerAttribute`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttribute.cs) and [`PlayerAttributeModifier`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttributeModifier.cs) are the ruleset loaded from `GameDetails.json`. - [`GameState`](Engine.Models/GameState.cs) is what gets saved: the `Player` plus the x/y coordinates. **Engine.Services** turns data files into model objects: - Each factory is a **static class** whose **static constructor** reads its XML file once and keeps "prototype" objects. The public methods return **clones**, so no two holders share state. - [`GameDetailService`](Engine.Services/GameDetailService.cs) parses `GameDetails.json` with Newtonsoft `JObject`. - [`SaveGameService`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs) serialises a `GameState` to JSON. On load, it rebuilds the `Player` and resolves items, quests and recipes **by ID** through the factories. **Engine.ViewModels** holds the state the UI binds to: - [`GameSession`](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs) is the running game. The heart of the game loop is the `CurrentLocation` setter; see the flowchart below. It exposes `MoveNorth/East/South/West`, `AttackCurrentMonster`, `UseCurrentConsumable` and `CraftItemUsing(recipe)`, plus `HasLocationToNorth/…`, `HasMonster` and `HasTrader` for button visibility. - [`CharacterCreationViewModel`](Engine.ViewModels/CharacterCreationViewModel.cs) rolls attributes, applies race modifiers, and builds the starting `Player` with its starter kit. **WPFUI** holds the views: - Windows are thin. Code-behind forwards button clicks and key presses to `GameSession` methods, and bindings display the state. - [`FileToBitmapConverter`](WPFUI/CustomConverters/FileToBitmapConverter.cs) turns an image path like `./Images/Monsters/Snake.png` into a cached `BitmapImage`, resolved against the `.exe` folder. ### Design patterns | Pattern | Where | Why | |---|---|---| | **MVVM** | `GameSession` / `CharacterCreationViewModel` are the windows' `DataContext` | The UI has no game logic, and the view models can be unit-tested without WPF. | | **Weaved `INotifyPropertyChanged`** | `FodyWeavers.xml` in Models and ViewModels (``) | Classes only declare `event PropertyChanged`. Fody injects the notify calls into every setter at compile time, including for computed properties that depend on them (`IsAlive`, `HasMonster`, `HasLocationToNorth`…). `[DoNotCheckEquality]` on `CurrentLocation` makes the setter run even when you "move" to the same location, for example respawning at Home while already there. | | **Factory + Prototype** | `ItemFactory`, `MonsterFactory`, … | Data is parsed once. Each request gets a `Clone()`, so two Snakes (or two Pointy sticks) never share HP, weapons or event subscribers. | | **Singleton** | `DiceService.Instance`, `MessageBroker.GetInstance()` | One random source and one message channel for the whole game. | | **Observer / events** | See the event table below | Loose coupling between actions, entities, battles, the session and the UI. | | **Strategy (pluggable behaviour)** | `GameItem.Action : IAction` | New item behaviours need no changes to `LivingEntity` or `Battle`. | | **Immutable object** | `Inventory` | Every change creates a new `Inventory` and assigns it to `LivingEntity.Inventory`. That single `PropertyChanged` refreshes every bound list: grids, weapon box, consumable box. | | **Disposable subscription** | `Battle : IDisposable` | When a monster is replaced, its old battle unhooks its handlers, so dead fights can't post messages. | | **Data-driven content** | `GameFiles/GameData` | Designers can add content without recompiling the engine; a rebuild just copies the If two monsters shared one weapon object, one monster's attack would be reported through the other monster's handlers as well. To avoid this: - `GameItem.Clone()` creates a new item **and** calls `Action.Clone(newItem)`, so every item instance has its own action and its own subscribers. - `Monster.Clone()` clones its weapon for every spawn. - The regression test `TestCombat.TwoHoldersOfTheSameItemTypeDoNotShareActionMessages` guards this. --- ## Adding or changing content All content lives in [`GameFiles/GameData`](GameFiles/GameData). After editing, **rebuild** so the files are copied next to the `.exe`. General rules: - **IDs must match across files.** A monster's `WeaponID`, a loot `ID`, a quest item, a recipe ingredient or a trader's stock must all exist in `GameItems.xml`. A missing ID fails at load time with `ArgumentException: ItemTypeId 'n' does not exist`. - **Element and attribute names are case-sensitive.** The factories use XPath such as `/GameItems/Weapons/Weapon`. - **Images** go in `GameFiles/Images/Locations` or `GameFiles/Images/Monsters` and are referenced by file name only. The UI draws them in a 125 × 125 box. - Every entity that fights needs a **`DEX`** attribute, because `Battle` and `AttackWithWeapon` call `GetAttribute("DEX")`. ### `GameDetails.json`: attributes and races ```json { "Name": "RPG", "Version": "0.1.000", "PlayerAttributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6" } ], "Races": [ { "Key": "ELF", "DisplayName": "Elf", "PlayerAttributeModifiers": [ { "Key": "CHA", "Modifier": "1" }, { "Key": "STR", "Modifier": "-1" } ] } ] } ``` | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `PlayerAttributes[].Key` | Short key used by code and modifiers (`DEX` is required for combat) | | `PlayerAttributes[].DiceNotation` | Any D20Tek notation, e.g. `3d6`, `4d6k3`, `2d8+2` | | `Races[]` | Optional. If there are none, the race picker is hidden. | | `PlayerAttributeModifiers[].Modifier` | Added to the rolled value to give `ModifiedValue` | ### `GameItems.xml`: items ```xml ``` | Element | Category | Extra attributes | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `Weapon` | Weapon | `DamageDice` (dice notation, required) | Gets an `AttackWithWeapon` action. Unique: shown one per row. | | `HealingItem` | Consumable | `HitPointsToHeal` (int) | Gets a `Heal` action. Used up when used. | | `MiscellaneousItem` | Miscellanous | — | Loot, quest items, crafting ingredients. | The ID ranges used so far are a convention, not a rule: 1xxx player weapons, 15xx monster weapons, 2xxx healing, 3xxx ingredients, 9xxx monster loot. ### `Monsters.xml`: monsters ```xml 15 ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `WeaponID` | Must be a **`Weapon`** item. Its `DamageDice` is the monster's damage. | | `RewardXP`, `Gold` | Given to the player when the monster dies | | `` | The monster's DEX (see [Known issues](#known-issues)) | | `LootItem Percentage` | Independent drop chance, 0–100, rolled when the monster spawns | ### `Locations.xml`: the world ```xml ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `X`, `Y` | Grid position. Must be unique. Neighbours are connected automatically. | | `Monsters/Monster Percent` | Relative spawn weight. With `Rat=75, Snake=25`, rats appear 3× as often. | | `Quests/Quest ID` | Quest offered **and** turned in here | | `Trader ID` | At most one trader per location | ### `Quests.xml`, `Recipes.xml` and `Traders.xml` ```xml ``` > `QuestFactory` silently loads nothing if `Quests.xml` is missing. Every other factory throws `FileNotFoundException`. ### Example: add a wolf and a new location 1. **`GameItems.xml`**: add a natural weapon and a loot item: ```xml ``` 2. **`Monsters.xml`**: add the monster: ```xml 13 ``` 3. **`Locations.xml`**: place it east of the Spider Forest, so the forest gets an *East* button automatically: ```xml ``` 4. Add `GameFiles/Images/Monsters/Wolf.png` and `GameFiles/Images/Locations/DarkWoods.png`. 5. Rebuild and run. --- ## Save files - **Saving.** Use *File → Save Game*, or answer *Yes* when closing the main window. A save dialog opens in the `.exe` folder with the filter `*.rpg`. - **Loading.** Use *Load saved game* on the Startup window. - **Format.** `SaveGameService` writes an indented JSON copy of `GameState`. Properties marked `[JsonIgnore]` are left out, so items, quests and recipes are stored **by ID only** and rebuilt from the factories on load. Example (abridged): ```json { "Player": { "CharacterClass": "Fighter", "Experience": 35, "Quests": [ { "Quest": { "Id": 1 }, "IsCompleted": false } ], "Recipes": [ { "ID": 1 } ], "Attributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 11, "ModifiedValue": 12 }, { "Key": "DEX", "DisplayName": "Dexterity", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 14, "ModifiedValue": 14 } ], "Name": "Jakob", "CurrentHitPoints": 8, "MaximumHitPoints": 10, "Gold": 17, "Level": 1, "Inventory": { "Items": [ { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 2001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 9001 } ] }, "CurrentWeapon": { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, "CurrentConsumable": null }, "XCoordinate": 0, "YCoordinate": 2 } ``` | Data | Saved | Restored on load | |---|:---:|:---:| | Name, class, XP (level is recalculated), max / current HP, gold | ✔ | ✔ | | Attributes (base and modified values; the race is already applied) | ✔ | ✔ | | Inventory (by `ItemTypeId`) | ✔ | ✔ | | Quests (ID + completed flag), known recipes (ID) | ✔ | ✔ | | Position (x, y) | ✔ | ✔ | | Equipped weapon / consumable | ✔ | ✘ (choose it again after loading) | | Trader stock and gold, the current monster | ✘ | ✘ (a new monster spawns on arrival) | A missing file throws `FileNotFoundException`. Any problem while reading the JSON is reported as `FormatException: Error reading: `. --- ## Tests ```powershell dotnet test rpg.sln # everything dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TestInventory" # one class dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "Name=EnoughAttacksKillsAMonster" # one test ``` The suite has 22 MSTest tests, and all pass. The test project's post-build step copies `GameFiles/` into its output folder, so the factories load the real game data. | Class (file) | Tests | What is covered | |---|:---:|---| | `TestAttackWithWeapon` ([Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs](Test/Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs)) | 3 | Valid construction. Throws `ArgumentException` for a non-weapon item or empty dice notation. | | `TestCombat` ([Models/TestCombat.cs](Test/Models/TestCombat.cs)) | 4 | Attacks reduce HP. Enough attacks kill (HP ends at exactly 0 and `OnKilled` fires). Consumables heal, are used up and are unequipped. Two monsters with the same weapon type don't share action messages. | | `TestInventory` ([Models/TestInventory.cs](Test/Models/TestInventory.cs)) | 9 | Empty inventory, add/remove single and multiple items, category views (`Weapons`, `Consumables`), removing by `ItemQuantity`, and removing more than you have (throws `InvalidOperationException`). | | `TestPlayer` ([Models/TestPlayer.cs](Test/Models/TestPlayer.cs)) | 4 | The constructor keeps the max HP it's given and doesn't raise `OnLeveledUp`. Level-up at 100 XP (max HP 20, event raised once). Selling the equipped weapon unequips it. | | `TestGameSession` ([ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs](Test/ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs)) | 2 | A new session starts at Home. Dying moves the player back Home fully healed. | Test helpers: - [`TestPlayerBuilder`](Test/TestPlayerBuilder.cs) creates players with **fixed** attribute values, so tests don't depend on dice rolls. `TestCombat` gives the player DEX 30, which pushes the hit chance above 100 %. - [`TestInventoryExtensions`](Test/TestInventoryExtensions.cs) adds factory-backed helpers (`AddItemFromFactory`, `AddItems(ItemQuantity…)`) that only the tests need, so `Inventory` itself stays independent of `ItemFactory`. --- ## Error handling and logging | Where | What happens | |---|---| | Factories | Missing data file → `FileNotFoundException`. Unknown ID → `ArgumentException`. Both are wrapped in `TypeInitializationException` when thrown from a static constructor. | | `AttackWithWeapon` / `Heal` constructors | `ArgumentException` if the item has the wrong category or the dice notation is empty | | `LivingEntity.SpendGold` | `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when spending more than you have. The trade window checks this first. | | `SaveGameService` | `FileNotFoundException` / `FormatException` | | `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` ([App.xaml.cs](WPFUI/App.xaml.cs)) | Logs the exception with `LoggingService` and shows a message box. **Note:** not wired up yet, see below. | | `LoggingService` | Appends to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`: timestamp, message, stack trace, then the same for every inner exception. | Log entry format: ``` EXCEPTION: 29.09.2026 14:03:12 ======================================== Object reference not set to an instance of an object. at Engine.ViewModels.GameSession.set_CurrentMonster(Monster value) ... INNER EXCEPTION ---------------------------------------- ... ``` --- ## Known issues I found these by reading the code. They are listed roughly by impact, each with a suggested fix. 1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity.** [`MonsterFactory.LoadMonstersFromNodes`](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs#L69-L78) writes each monster's `` into the **same** shared `PlayerAttribute` objects and passes them to every `Monster`. [`Monster.Clone`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs#L29) then shares them again. As a result, all monsters end up with the last value loaded, the Giant Spider's 12. *Fix:* create new `PlayerAttribute` instances per monster, and copy them in `Clone()`. 2. **Possible crash when a monster kills you the moment you arrive.** If a monster wins initiative, it attacks inside the `Battle` constructor. If that attack kills the player, `OnPlayerKilled` moves them Home. That sets `CurrentMonster = null` while `_currentBattle` is still `null`, and [the setter](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs#L66-L71) dereferences it, which throws a `NullReferenceException`. The easiest way to hit this is to walk into the Spider Forest with 1–2 HP. *Fix:* start the first attack after `GameSession` has stored the battle (e.g. a separate `Battle.Start()`), and null-check `_currentBattle`. 3. **The unhandled-exception logger is never called.** `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` exists, but [`App.xaml`](WPFUI/App.xaml#L1-L6) doesn't hook it up. As a result, errors crash the app and nothing is written to `Logs/`. *Fix:* add `DispatcherUnhandledException="App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException"` to the `` element. 4. **The consumable controls are always visible.** [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L249) binds to `Inventory.HasConsumables`, but the property is called `HasConsumable`. The binding fails, so the visibility falls back to *Visible*. 5. **Overlapping rows in the player panel.** In [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L55-L85), *Experience* (row 5), *Gold* (row 6, which is clamped to row 5 because the grid has only 6 rows) and the attribute list (row 5) share one grid row and are drawn on top of each other. 6. **The Startup window has no title.** [`Startup.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/Startup.xaml#L11) binds `Title` to `GameDetails.Title`, which doesn't exist. `GameDetails.Name` was probably meant. 7. **The equipped weapon isn't restored after loading.** It is saved, but [`SaveGameService.CreatePlayer`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs#L39-L55) never reads it back. Select a weapon again after loading. 8. **T opens the trade screen even where there is no trader.** The result is an empty trade window. The hotkey should check `HasTrader` first ([MainWindow.xaml.cs](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L90)). 9. **A stale test file.** [`Test/Services/TestCombatServices`](Test/Services/TestCombatServices) has no `.cs` extension and refers to a `CombatService` class that no longer exists, so it isn't compiled. Delete it, or port it to `Battle`. 10. **`RPGState.json` is a save file from an older version.** It uses `CurrentPlayer` / `CurrentLocation` keys and cannot be loaded by the current `SaveGameService`, which expects `Player` / `XCoordinate` / `YCoordinate` in a `.rpg` file. 11. **Content typo.** The Farmer's House description mentions "Farmer **Fred**", but the trader there is "Farmer **Ted**". --- ## Limitations and ideas - Only **DEX** is used by the rules. STR could scale damage, CON could raise max HP, and CHA could affect trade prices. - **Recipes can only be learned in code** (`CharacterCreationViewModel.GetPlayer`). A recipe reward on quests or a recipe trader would open up crafting. - All three traders only stock a Pointy stick, so **crafting ingredients can't be bought** once the starting ones are used. - There is **no armour** and no defence value. Hit chance depends only on DEX. - **Levelling up doesn't heal**, and `CharacterClass` is always `"Fighter"`. - The *Help* and *About* menu items are placeholders (disabled). - **Traders aren't saved**, and they keep their state across new games in the same app session. - Windows-only: WPF plus the `xcopy` post-build step. --- ## Credits - The game's structure and starter content follow **Scott Lilly's "Build a C#/WPF RPG" tutorial series (SOSCSRPG)**. The commit history tracks progress through its lessons. - Libraries used: - [D20Tek.DiceNotation](https://github.com/d20Tek/DiceNotation) for dice rolling. - [Fody](https://github.com/Fody/Fody) / [PropertyChanged.Fody](https://github.com/Fody/PropertyChanged) for automatic `INotifyPropertyChanged`. - [Newtonsoft.Json](https://www.newtonsoft.com/json) for JSON. - [MSTest](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx) for tests.

# Jakob's RPG A turn-based, tile-based role-playing game for Windows, written in **C# on .NET 9** with **WPF** and the **MVVM** pattern. You create a character, explore a small town, fight monsters, collect loot, finish quests, craft items and trade with shopkeepers. The game's content is loaded from XML/JSON files at startup: locations, monsters, items, quests, recipes, traders, races and attributes. You can add new content without touching the C# code.

--- ## Contents 1. [Features](#features) 2. [Getting started](#getting-started) 3. [How to play](#how-to-play) 4. [World map](#world-map) 5. [Game rules and formulas](#game-rules-and-formulas) 6. [Game content reference](#game-content-reference) 7. [Architecture](#architecture) 8. [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content) 9. [Save files](#save-files) 10. [Tests](#tests) 11. [Error handling and logging](#error-handling-and-logging) 12. [Known issues](#known-issues) 13. [Limitations and ideas](#limitations-and-ideas) 14. [Credits](#credits) --- ## Features | Area | What it does | |---|---| | **Character creation** | Choose a name and a race (Human, Elf, Orc). Six attributes are rolled with `3d6`, then race modifiers are applied. You can re-roll as often as you like. | | **Exploration** | A 9-location grid world. You move north, east, south or west with buttons or the `W` `A` `S` `D` keys. A direction button only appears when a location exists in that direction. | | **Combat** | Turn-based. Initiative and hit chance come from Dexterity plus a random roll, and damage comes from the weapon's dice notation (e.g. `1d4`). | | **Loot and progression** | Monsters drop gold, experience and items from a per-monster loot table. Every 100 XP gives you a level and raises your maximum HP. | | **Quests** | You receive a quest automatically when you enter the location that offers it. You complete it automatically when you come back with the required items. | | **Crafting** | Turn ingredients into items with recipes you know (e.g. Oats + Honey + Raisins → Granola bar). | | **Trading** | Buy and sell items with three traders at the item's listed price. | | **Consumables** | Healing items restore hit points and are used up. | | **Save / load** | Save to a `.rpg` file (JSON) and load it again from the start screen. You are asked whether to save every time the game window closes. | | **Death** | When you die you wake up at Home with full health. You keep your items, gold and XP. | | **Data-driven** | All content lives in [`GameFiles/GameData`](GameFiles/GameData). See [Adding or changing content](#adding-or-changing-content). | --- ## Getting started ### Requirements - **Windows 10 or 11**. WPF only runs on Windows, and the build's post-build step uses `xcopy`. - **.NET 9 SDK**. Built and tested with SDK `9.0.318`. - Optional: **Visual Studio 2022** (17.12 or later), or **VS Code** with the C# Dev Kit extension. ### Build, run and test From the repository root: ```powershell # Restore NuGet packages and build every project dotnet build rpg.sln # Start the game dotnet run --project WPFUI # Run the unit tests (22 tests, MSTest) dotnet test rpg.sln ``` In Visual Studio, open `rpg.sln`, set **WPFUI** as the startup project and press F5. > The build currently reports about 100 nullable-reference warnings (`CS86xx`) and no errors. They do not affect the game. ### How the game finds its data `WPFUI.csproj` and `Test/test.csproj` both have a post-build step that copies the whole `GameFiles/` folder into the build output: ```xml ``` After a build, the output folder (for example `WPFUI/bin/Debug/net9.0-windows/`) contains `GameData/*.xml`, `GameData/GameDetails.json` and `Images/**`. Every factory builds its path from `AppContext.BaseDirectory`, which is the folder containing the `.exe`, not the current working directory. That's why the game and the tests find their data no matter where they are started from. > **After editing anything in `GameFiles/`, rebuild** so the copy in `bin/` is refreshed. --- ## How to play ### Starting a game ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Startup Startup --> CharacterCreation: Start New Game Startup --> MainWindow: Load saved game (.rpg) Startup --> [*]: Exit CharacterCreation --> CharacterCreation: Roll new player CharacterCreation --> MainWindow: Use this player MainWindow --> TradeWindow: Trade button or T (modal) TradeWindow --> MainWindow: Close MainWindow --> SavePrompt: window closes (File → Exit, X button, File → New Game) SavePrompt --> [*]: Yes (save dialog) or No MainWindow --> Startup: File → New Game ``` 1. **Startup window.** Choose *Start New Game*, *Load saved game* or *Exit*. 2. **Character creation.** Type a name and pick a race. The attribute table shows the rolled **Value** and the **Modified** value after the race bonus. Click *Roll new player* to re-roll, or *Use this player* to begin. Every new character starts with: | | | |---|---| | Class | Fighter | | Level / XP | 1 / 0 | | Hit points | 10 / 10 | | Gold | 10 | | Location | Town Square (0, 0) | | Inventory | Pointy stick, Granola bar, Oats, Honey, Raisins | | Known recipes | Granola bar | ### The main screen ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ File: New Game · Save Game · Exit Help: Help · About (disabled) │ ├────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┤ │ PLAYER │ MESSAGE LOG │ LOCATION │ │ Name │ everything that happens: │ name · picture · │ │ Level │ combat, loot, quests, │ description │ │ Health │ crafting, level-ups ├─────────────────────────┤ │ Experience │ │ MONSTER │ │ Gold │ │ name · picture · │ │ Attributes │ │ health │ ├────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┤ │ [Inventory] │ Weapon ▾ [Use] [North] │ │ [Quests] │ Consumable ▾ [Use] [West] [Trade] [East] │ │ [Recipes] │ [South] │ └────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` - **Inventory tab.** Your items grouped by type with quantity and price. Weapons are listed one per row because each is unique. - **Quests tab.** Your quests and whether they are done. Hover over a quest name to see what to bring and what you'll get. - **Recipes tab.** Known recipes. Hover to see ingredients and output. *Craft* makes one batch. - **Weapon / Attack.** The weapon box and its *Use* button only appear while a monster is present. - **Movement pad.** A direction button is only shown if there is a location in that direction. *Trade* appears when a trader is at your location. ### Controls | Action | Mouse | Keyboard | |---|---|---| | Move north / west / south / east | Direction buttons | W / A / S / D | | Attack the current monster | Choose a weapon, click *Use* | K | | Use the selected consumable | Choose a consumable, click *Use* | C | | Show Inventory / Quests / Recipes tab | Click the tab | I / Q / R | | Open the trade screen | *Trade* | T | | Craft an item | *Craft* in the Recipes tab | — | | Save | *File → Save Game* | — | | New game | *File → New Game* | — | | Quit | *File → Exit* or close the window (asks to save) | — | ### Your first quest: a walkthrough 1. **Equip a weapon.** You start with nothing equipped. Pick *Pointy stick* in the weapon box. Until you do, attacking only prints *"You must select a weapon, to attack"*. 2. From Town Square go **north** to the **Herbalist's Hut** (0, 1). You receive the quest **"Clear the herb garden"**: bring back **5 Snake fangs**. 3. Go **north** again to the **Herbalist's Garden** (0, 2) and fight snakes. Each snake has a **25%** chance to drop a Snake fang and a 75% chance to drop Snakeskin, so expect to fight about 20 snakes. A new snake appears as soon as you kill one. 4. **Heal** with your Granola bar when HP gets low. You start with ingredients for one more, which you can craft in the Recipes tab. 5. Walk back **south** into the Herbalist's Hut with 5 fangs. The quest completes automatically: **25 XP, 10 gold and a Rusty sword** (`1d3` damage, better than the Pointy stick's `1d2`). 6. **Sell** your extra loot (Snakeskin, Rat fur, Spider silk…) to any trader. 7. When you're ready, head east through the Town Gate to the **Spider Forest**. Giant spiders have more HP and hit harder (`1d4`). --- ## World map North is `y + 1`, east is `x + 1`.
