Game rules always use `ModifiedValue`. | Race | Modifiers | |---|---| | Human | CON +1 | | Elf | CHA +1, STR −1 | | Orc | STR +1, CHA −1 | > Only **Dexterity** affects gameplay at the moment, through initiative and hit chance. The other attributes are shown but not used yet. ### Experience and levels ``` Level = Experience / 100 + 1 (integer division) MaximumHitPoints = Level × 10 (set only when the level changes) ``` | Experience | Level | Max HP after reaching it | |---|---|---| | 0 – 99 | 1 | 10 (starting value) | | 100 – 199 | 2 | 20 | | 200 – 299 | 3 | 30 | | … | n | n × 10 | Levelling up raises your **maximum** HP but not your current HP. The message log shows *"You are now Level n"*. ### Combat 1. **Encounter.** When you enter a location that has monsters, one is picked at random. The `Percent` values in `Locations.xml` are **relative weights**, so they don't have to add up to 100. Each spawn is a fresh copy with its own weapon. Its loot is rolled at spawn time: each loot-table entry drops independently if `d100 ≤ Percentage`. 2. **Initiative.** A `Battle` starts immediately. If the monster wins initiative, **it attacks you the moment you arrive**. 3. **Your turn.** Each attack you make is resolved first. If the monster survives, it attacks back once. 4. **Hit check.** The same formula is used for initiative and for every attack: ``` dexOffset = (attackerDEX² − defenderDEX²) / 10 randomOffset = d20 − 10 // −9 … +10 success = d100 ≤ 50 + dexOffset + randomOffset ``` | Attacker DEX | Defender DEX | Chance to hit / go first | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | 10 | 10 | 41 % – 60 % | | 14 | 10 | 50 % – 69 % | | 18 | 3 | 72 % – 91 % | | 3 | 18 | 9 % – 28 % | 5. **Damage.** On a hit, the weapon's `DamageDice` are rolled (e.g. `1d2`). A creature at 0 HP or less is set to exactly 0 and dies. 6. **Victory.** You receive the monster's XP, gold and every item in its inventory. **A new monster of that location spawns immediately**, so fights chain until you leave. 7. **Fleeing.** Just walk away; the battle is thrown away. When you come back, a new monster is spawned. 8. **Consumables in combat.** Using a consumable does **not** give the monster a turn. ### Healing A healing item restores its `HitPointsToHeal`, capped at your maximum HP, and is then removed from your inventory. The only healing item is the **Granola bar** (+2 HP). ### Quests - **Receiving.** When you enter a location, you get every quest it offers that you don't already have. The message log lists the required items and the rewards. - **Completing.** Also when you enter that location. If you have all the required items, they are taken from you and you get the XP, gold and reward items. The quest is then marked *Done*. - The game checks for completions **before** it hands out new quests. So a quest can't be finished on the same visit you receive it. Step out and come back in. ### Crafting *Craft* checks that you have every ingredient in the required quantity. If you do, the ingredients are removed and the output items are added. If not, the message log lists what's needed. New recipes can only be learned in code for now; see [Limitations](#limitations-and-ideas). ### Trading - *Buy* and *Sell 1* use the item's `Price` in both directions, with no markup. - Each trader starts with **9999 gold** and will refuse a sale they can't afford. - If you sell your equipped weapon or consumable, it is unequipped. - Trader stock and gold live in memory for as long as the app runs. They are shared across new games in the same session and are **not** saved. ### Death and respawn When your HP reaches 0 the log shows *"You have been killed"*. You are moved to **Home (0, −1)** and healed to full. You keep your inventory, gold, XP and quests. --- ## Game content reference ### Items — [`GameItems.xml`](GameFiles/GameData/GameItems.xml) | ID | Name | Category | Price | Effect / use | |---:|---|---|---:|---| | 1001 | Pointy stick | Weapon | 1 | `1d2` damage · starting weapon, sold by every trader | | 1002 | Rusty sword | Weapon | 5 | `1d3` damage · quest reward | | 1501 | Snake fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Snake's natural weapon | | 1502 | Rat claw | Weapon | 0 | `1d2` · the Rat's natural weapon | | 1503 | Spider fang | Weapon | 0 | `1d4` · the Giant Spider's natural weapon | | 2001 | Granola bar | Consumable | 5 | Heals 2 HP · craftable | | 3001 | Oats | Miscellaneous | 1 | Crafting ingredient | | 3002 | Honey | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 3003 | Raisins | Miscellaneous | 2 | Crafting ingredient | | 9001 | Snake fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Snake loot · **quest item** | | 9002 | Snakeskin | Miscellaneous | 2 | Snake loot | | 9003 | Rat tail | Miscellaneous | 1 | Rat loot | | 9004 | Rat fur | Miscellaneous | 2 | Rat loot | | 9005 | Spider fang | Miscellaneous | 1 | Spider loot | | 9006 | Spider silk | Miscellaneous | 2 | Spider loot | The 15xx "natural weapons" and the 9xxx loot items can share a name. ### Layers in detail **Engine.Core** holds infrastructure with no game rules: - [`DiceService`](Engine.Core/DiceService.cs) is a singleton (`DiceService.Instance`) over the D20Tek library. It accepts dice notation (`Roll("3d6")`) or sides/count/modifier (`Roll(100)`). `Configure(RollerType.Constant, constantValue: n)` swaps in a fixed roller, which is useful for deterministic tests. - [`MessageBroker`](Engine.Core/MessageBroker.cs) is a singleton (`MessageBroker.GetInstance()`). Game code calls `RaiseMessage(text)`, and the UI listens to `OnMessageRaised`. This keeps the game logic from ever referencing a WPF control. - [`LoggingService`](Engine.Core/LoggingService.cs) is static. It writes an exception, and recursively its inner exceptions, to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`. **Engine.Models** holds the domain: - [`LivingEntity`](Engine.Models/LivingEntity.cs) is the abstract base for anything with HP, gold, a level, attributes and an inventory. It exposes `TakeDamage`, `Heal`, `CompleteHeal`, `ReceiveGold`, `SpendGold`, `AddItemToInventory`, `RemoveItemFromInventory`, `UseCurrentWeaponOn(target)` and `UseCurrentConsumable()`. It raises `OnKilled` and relays its equipped item's action text as `OnActionPerformed`. - [`Player`](Engine.Models/Player.cs) adds `Experience`, `CharacterClass`, `Quests`, `Recipes`, `AddExperience` (with level-up) and `LearnRecipe`. - [`Monster`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs) adds `ID`, `ImageName`, `RewardedExperiencePoints` and a `LootTable`. `Clone()` gives every spawn its own weapon. - [`Trader`](Engine.Models/Trader.cs) is a `LivingEntity` with 9999 HP and gold and no attributes. - [`GameItem`](Engine.Models/GameItem.cs) has a `Category` (Weapon, Consumable, Miscellanous), an `ItemTypeId`, `Name`, `Price`, `IsUnique` and an optional `IAction`. Its `Clone()` also clones the action and binds it to the new item. - [`IAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/IAction.cs) has two implementations. [`AttackWithWeapon`](Engine.Models/Actions/AttackWithWeapon.cs) does a hit roll, then rolls damage dice. [`Heal`](Engine.Models/Actions/Heal.cs) restores HP. Both inherit [`BaseAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/BaseActions.cs), which raises `OnActionPerformed` with a human-readable result. - [`Inventory`](Engine.Models/Inventory.cs) is immutable. `AddItem(s)` and `RemoveItem(s)` return a **new** `Inventory`. It exposes `Items`, `GroupedInventory` (for the grids), `Weapons`, `Consumables`, `HasConsumable` and `HasAllTheseItems(...)`. - [`Battle`](Engine.Models/Battle.cs) owns one fight. It subscribes to both combatants' events, rolls initiative, runs the attack → counter-attack exchange, hands out rewards and raises `OnCombatVictory`. It is `IDisposable` so it can unhook its event handlers. - [`World`](Engine.Models/World.cs) and [`Location`](Engine.Models/Location.cs) form the grid. `LocationAt(x, y)` finds a location. Each location has a name, description, image, `MonstersHere` (weighted), `QuestsAvailableHere` and `TraderHere`. - [`Quest`](Engine.Models/Quest.cs) / [`QuestStatus`](Engine.Models/QuestStatus.cs) / [`Recipe`](Engine.Models/Recipe.cs) are built from [`ItemQuantity`](Engine.Models/ItemQuantity.cs) lists. They also build the tooltip text shown in the UI. - [`GameDetails`](Engine.Models/GameDetails.cs), [`Race`](Engine.Models/Race.cs), [`PlayerAttribute`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttribute.cs) and [`PlayerAttributeModifier`](Engine.Models/PlayerAttributeModifier.cs) are the ruleset loaded from `GameDetails.json`. - [`GameState`](Engine.Models/GameState.cs) is what gets saved: the `Player` plus the x/y coordinates. **Engine.Services** turns data files into model objects: - Each factory is a **static class** whose **static constructor** reads its XML file once and keeps "prototype" objects. The public methods return **clones**, so no two holders share state. - [`GameDetailService`](Engine.Services/GameDetailService.cs) parses `GameDetails.json` with Newtonsoft `JObject`. - [`SaveGameService`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs) serialises a `GameState` to JSON. On load, it rebuilds the `Player` and resolves items, quests and recipes **by ID** through the factories. **Engine.ViewModels** holds the state the UI binds to: - [`GameSession`](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs) is the running game. The heart of the game loop is the `CurrentLocation` setter; see the flowchart below. It exposes `MoveNorth/East/South/West`, `AttackCurrentMonster`, `UseCurrentConsumable` and `CraftItemUsing(recipe)`, plus `HasLocationToNorth/…`, `HasMonster` and `HasTrader` for button visibility. - [`CharacterCreationViewModel`](Engine.ViewModels/CharacterCreationViewModel.cs) rolls attributes, applies race modifiers, and builds the starting `Player` with its starter kit. **WPFUI** holds the views: - Windows are thin. Code-behind forwards button clicks and key presses to `GameSession` methods, and bindings display the state. - [`FileToBitmapConverter`](WPFUI/CustomConverters/FileToBitmapConverter.cs) turns an image path like `./Images/Monsters/Snake.png` into a cached `BitmapImage`, resolved against the `.exe` folder. ### Design patterns | Pattern | Where | Why | |---|---|---| | **MVVM** | `GameSession` / `CharacterCreationViewModel` are the windows' `DataContext` | The UI has no game logic, and the view models can be unit-tested without WPF. | | **Weaved `INotifyPropertyChanged`** | `FodyWeavers.xml` in Models and ViewModels (``) | Classes only declare `event PropertyChanged`. Fody injects the notify calls into every setter at compile time, including for computed properties that depend on them (`IsAlive`, `HasMonster`, `HasLocationToNorth`…). `[DoNotCheckEquality]` on `CurrentLocation` makes the setter run even when you "move" to the same location, for example respawning at Home while already there. | | **Factory + Prototype** | `ItemFactory`, `MonsterFactory`, … | Data is parsed once. Each request gets a `Clone()`, so two Snakes (or two Pointy sticks) never share HP, weapons or event subscribers. | | **Singleton** | `DiceService.Instance`, `MessageBroker.GetInstance()` | One random source and one message channel for the whole game. | | **Observer / events** | See the event table below | Loose coupling between actions, entities, battles, the session and the UI. | | **Strategy (pluggable behaviour)** | `GameItem.Action : IAction` | New item behaviours need no changes to `LivingEntity` or `Battle`. | | **Immutable object** | `Inventory` | Every change creates a new `Inventory` and assigns it to `LivingEntity.Inventory`. That single `PropertyChanged` refreshes every bound list: grids, weapon box, consumable box. | | **Disposable subscription** | `Battle : IDisposable` | When a monster is replaced, its old battle unhooks its handlers, so dead fights can't post messages. | | **Data-driven content** | `GameFiles/GameData` | Designers can add content without recompiling the engine; a rebuild just copies the everything in the game happens in the `GameSession.CurrentLocation` setter. It runs on every move, on respawn and when a game is loaded. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Player presses a direction
(or dies, or a game starts)"] --> B{"Location at
target (x, y)?"} B -->|no| Z["Nothing happens"] B -->|yes| C["CurrentLocation = destination"] C --> D["CompleteQuestsAtLocation()
for each quest offered here that the player has open:
has all items? → remove them, grant XP, gold, reward items, mark Done"] D --> E["GivePlayerQuestsAtLocation()
add any quest offered here that the player doesn't have yet"] E --> F{"MonstersHere
empty?"} F -->|yes| G["CurrentMonster = null
(old Battle disposed)"] F -->|no| H["MonsterFactory.GetMonsterFromLocation()
weighted pick → Clone() → roll loot"] H --> I["CurrentMonster = monster
new Battle(player, monster)"] I --> J{"Initiative roll"} J -->|monster first| K["Monster attacks immediately"] J -->|player first| L["Wait for the player"] G --> M["CurrentTrader = location.TraderHere"] K --> M L --> M M --> N["Fody raises PropertyChanged
→ buttons, panels and pictures update"] ``` ### Combat, step by step What happens when you click **Use** next to the weapon box (or press K): ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User participant MW as MainWindow participant GS as GameSession participant B as Battle participant P as Player participant A as AttackWithWeapon
(weapon's action) participant M as Monster participant MB as MessageBroker User->>MW: click Use / press K MW->>GS: AttackCurrentMonster() GS->>B: AttackOpponent() alt no weapon equipped B->>MB: RaiseMessage(select a weapon first) else weapon equipped B->>P: UseCurrentWeaponOn(monster) P->>A: GameItem.PerformAction → Execute(player, monster) A->>A: hit check (d100 vs 50 + DEX offset + d20 − 10) A-->>P: OnActionPerformed("PLAYER hit snake for 2 points") P-->>B: OnActionPerformed (relayed) B->>MB: RaiseMessage(text) MB-->>MW: OnMessageRaised → append line to log A->>M: TakeDamage(damage roll) alt monster dies M-->>B: OnKilled B->>P: AddExperience · ReceiveGold · AddItemToInventory(loot) B->>MB: RaiseMessage(victory, XP, gold, items) B-->>GS: OnCombatVictory GS->>GS: CurrentMonster = new spawn (new Battle) else monster survives B->>M: UseCurrentWeaponOn(player) Note over M,P: Same flow in reverse. If the player dies,
GameSession.OnPlayerKilled moves them Home and heals them. end end ``` ### Content pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Disk["bin/…/GameData (copied from GameFiles/ on build)"] J["GameDetails.json"] I["GameItems.xml"] Mo["Monsters.xml"] Q["Quests.xml"] R["Recipes.xml"] T["Traders.xml"] L["Locations.xml"] end I --> IF["ItemFactory
prototype items + actions"] J --> GDS["GameDetailService"] Mo --> MF["MonsterFactory
prototype monsters"] GDS --> MF IF --> MF Q --> QF["QuestFactory"] IF --> QF R --> RF["RecipeFactory"] IF --> RF T --> TF["TraderFactory
traders + stock"] IF --> TF L --> WF["WorldFactory"] QF --> WF TF --> WF WF --> World["World
(one per GameSession)"] MF --> Spawn["Monster clones
(one per encounter)"] IF --> Items["GameItem clones
(one per item instance)"] GDS --> CC["CharacterCreationViewModel
attributes + races"] ``` The static constructors run on first use. As a result, a missing or malformed file surfaces as a `TypeInitializationException` wrapping the real `FileNotFoundException` or `ArgumentException`, the first time that factory is touched. ### Events and messages | Event | Declared in | Raised when | Handled by | |---|---|---|---| | `MessageBroker.OnMessageRaised` | Engine.Core | Anything calls `RaiseMessage(text)` | `MainWindow` appends a paragraph to the message log and scrolls to the end | | `IAction.OnActionPerformed` | `BaseAction` | An action finishes (`"X hit Y for 2 points"`) | The `LivingEntity` that has that item equipped | | `LivingEntity.OnActionPerformed` | `LivingEntity` | Relays its equipped item's action text | `Battle` (for both combatants). `GameSession` subscribes briefly when a consumable is used outside combat. | | `LivingEntity.OnKilled` | `LivingEntity` | HP drops to 0 | `Battle` (monster died → rewards). `GameSession` (player died → respawn). | | `Player.OnLeveledUp` | `Player` | `AddExperience` changes the level | `GameSession` → *"You are now Level n"* | | `Battle.OnCombatVictory` | `Battle` | After rewards are handed out | `GameSession` → spawns the next monster | | `PropertyChanged` | Every model/view-model class (woven by Fody) | Any property setter | WPF data bindings | ### Why items and monsters are cloned A `GameItem`'s `IAction` raises `OnActionPerformed`, and the entity holding the item subscribes to it. If two monsters shared one weapon object, one monster's attack would be reported through the other monster's handlers as well. To avoid this: - `GameItem.Clone()` creates a new item **and** calls `Action.Clone(newItem)`, so every item instance has its own action and its own subscribers. - `Monster.Clone()` clones its weapon for every spawn. - The regression test `TestCombat.TwoHoldersOfTheSameItemTypeDoNotShareActionMessages` guards this. --- ## Adding or changing content All content lives in [`GameFiles/GameData`](GameFiles/GameData). After editing, **rebuild** so the files are copied next to the `.exe`. General rules: - **IDs must match across files.** A monster's `WeaponID`, a loot `ID`, a quest item, a recipe ingredient or a trader's stock must all exist in `GameItems.xml`. A missing ID fails at load time with `ArgumentException: ItemTypeId 'n' does not exist`. - **Element and attribute names are case-sensitive.** The factories use XPath such as `/GameItems/Weapons/Weapon`. - **Images** go in `GameFiles/Images/Locations` or `GameFiles/Images/Monsters` and are referenced by file name only. The UI draws them in a 125 × 125 box. - Every entity that fights needs a **`DEX`** attribute, because `Battle` and `AttackWithWeapon` call `GetAttribute("DEX")`. ### `GameDetails.json`: attributes and races ```json { "Name": "RPG", "Version": "0.1.000", "PlayerAttributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6" } ], "Races": [ { "Key": "ELF", "DisplayName": "Elf", "PlayerAttributeModifiers": [ { "Key": "CHA", "Modifier": "1" }, { "Key": "STR", "Modifier": "-1" } ] } ] } ``` | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `PlayerAttributes[].Key` | Short key used by code and modifiers (`DEX` is required for combat) | | `PlayerAttributes[].DiceNotation` | Any D20Tek notation, e.g. `3d6`, `4d6k3`, `2d8+2` | | `Races[]` | Optional. If there are none, the race picker is hidden. | | `PlayerAttributeModifiers[].Modifier` | Added to the rolled value to give `ModifiedValue` | ### `GameItems.xml`: items ```xml ``` | Element | Category | Extra attributes | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `Weapon` | Weapon | `DamageDice` (dice notation, required) | Gets an `AttackWithWeapon` action. Unique: shown one per row. | | `HealingItem` | Consumable | `HitPointsToHeal` (int) | Gets a `Heal` action. Used up when used. | | `MiscellaneousItem` | Miscellanous | — | Loot, quest items, crafting ingredients. | The ID ranges used so far are a convention, not a rule: 1xxx player weapons, 15xx monster weapons, 2xxx healing, 3xxx ingredients, 9xxx monster loot. ### `Monsters.xml`: monsters ```xml 15 ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `WeaponID` | Must be a **`Weapon`** item. Its `DamageDice` is the monster's damage. | | `RewardXP`, `Gold` | Given to the player when the monster dies | | `` | The monster's DEX (see [Known issues](#known-issues)) | | `LootItem Percentage` | Independent drop chance, 0–100, rolled when the monster spawns | ### `Locations.xml`: the world ```xml ``` | Attribute / element | Meaning | |---|---| | `X`, `Y` | Grid position. Must be unique. Neighbours are connected automatically. | | `Monsters/Monster Percent` | Relative spawn weight. With `Rat=75, Snake=25`, rats appear 3× as often. | | `Quests/Quest ID` | Quest offered **and** turned in here | | `Trader ID` | At most one trader per location | ### `Quests.xml`, `Recipes.xml` and `Traders.xml` ```xml ``` > `QuestFactory` silently loads nothing if `Quests.xml` is missing. Every other factory throws `FileNotFoundException`. ### Example: add a wolf and a new location 1. **`GameItems.xml`**: add a natural weapon and a loot item: ```xml ``` 2. **`Monsters.xml`**: add the monster: ```xml 13 ``` 3. **`Locations.xml`**: place it east of the Spider Forest, so the forest gets an *East* button automatically: ```xml ``` 4. Add `GameFiles/Images/Monsters/Wolf.png` and `GameFiles/Images/Locations/DarkWoods.png`. 5. Rebuild and run. --- ## Save files - **Saving.** Use *File → Save Game*, or answer *Yes* when closing the main window. A save dialog opens in the `.exe` folder with the filter `*.rpg`. - **Loading.** Use *Load saved game* on the Startup window. - **Format.** `SaveGameService` writes an indented JSON copy of `GameState`. Properties marked `[JsonIgnore]` are left out, so items, quests and recipes are stored **by ID only** and rebuilt from the factories on load. Example (abridged): ```json { "Player": { "CharacterClass": "Fighter", "Experience": 35, "Quests": [ { "Quest": { "Id": 1 }, "IsCompleted": false } ], "Recipes": [ { "ID": 1 } ], "Attributes": [ { "Key": "STR", "DisplayName": "Strength", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 11, "ModifiedValue": 12 }, { "Key": "DEX", "DisplayName": "Dexterity", "DiceNotation": "3d6", "BaseValue": 14, "ModifiedValue": 14 } ], "Name": "Jakob", "CurrentHitPoints": 8, "MaximumHitPoints": 10, "Gold": 17, "Level": 1, "Inventory": { "Items": [ { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 2001 }, { "ItemTypeId": 9001 } ] }, "CurrentWeapon": { "ItemTypeId": 1001 }, "CurrentConsumable": null }, "XCoordinate": 0, "YCoordinate": 2 } ``` | Data | Saved | Restored on load | |---|:---:|:---:| | Name, class, XP (level is recalculated), max / current HP, gold | ✔ | ✔ | | Attributes (base and modified values; the race is already applied) | ✔ | ✔ | | Inventory (by `ItemTypeId`) | ✔ | ✔ | | Quests (ID + completed flag), known recipes (ID) | ✔ | ✔ | | Position (x, y) | ✔ | ✔ | | Equipped weapon / consumable | ✔ | ✘ (choose it again after loading) | | Trader stock and gold, the current monster | ✘ | ✘ (a new monster spawns on arrival) | A missing file throws `FileNotFoundException`. Any problem while reading the JSON is reported as `FormatException: Error reading: `. --- ## Tests ```powershell dotnet test rpg.sln # everything dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TestInventory" # one class dotnet test rpg.sln --filter "Name=EnoughAttacksKillsAMonster" # one test ``` The suite has 22 MSTest tests, and all pass. The test project's post-build step copies `GameFiles/` into its output folder, so the factories load the real game data. | Class (file) | Tests | What is covered | |---|:---:|---| | `TestAttackWithWeapon` ([Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs](Test/Actions/TestWithWeapon.cs)) | 3 | Valid construction. Throws `ArgumentException` for a non-weapon item or empty dice notation. | | `TestCombat` ([Models/TestCombat.cs](Test/Models/TestCombat.cs)) | 4 | Attacks reduce HP. Enough attacks kill (HP ends at exactly 0 and `OnKilled` fires). Consumables heal, are used up and are unequipped. Two monsters with the same weapon type don't share action messages. | | `TestInventory` ([Models/TestInventory.cs](Test/Models/TestInventory.cs)) | 9 | Empty inventory, add/remove single and multiple items, category views (`Weapons`, `Consumables`), removing by `ItemQuantity`, and removing more than you have (throws `InvalidOperationException`). | | `TestPlayer` ([Models/TestPlayer.cs](Test/Models/TestPlayer.cs)) | 4 | The constructor keeps the max HP it's given and doesn't raise `OnLeveledUp`. Level-up at 100 XP (max HP 20, event raised once). Selling the equipped weapon unequips it. | | `TestGameSession` ([ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs](Test/ViewModels/TestGameSession.cs)) | 2 | A new session starts at Home. Dying moves the player back Home fully healed. | Test helpers: - [`TestPlayerBuilder`](Test/TestPlayerBuilder.cs) creates players with **fixed** attribute values, so tests don't depend on dice rolls. `TestCombat` gives the player DEX 30, which pushes the hit chance above 100 %. - [`TestInventoryExtensions`](Test/TestInventoryExtensions.cs) adds factory-backed helpers (`AddItemFromFactory`, `AddItems(ItemQuantity…)`) that only the tests need, so `Inventory` itself stays independent of `ItemFactory`. --- ## Error handling and logging | Where | What happens | |---|---| | Factories | Missing data file → `FileNotFoundException`. Unknown ID → `ArgumentException`. Both are wrapped in `TypeInitializationException` when thrown from a static constructor. | | `AttackWithWeapon` / `Heal` constructors | `ArgumentException` if the item has the wrong category or the dice notation is empty | | `LivingEntity.SpendGold` | `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when spending more than you have. The trade window checks this first. | | `SaveGameService` | `FileNotFoundException` / `FormatException` | | `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` ([App.xaml.cs](WPFUI/App.xaml.cs)) | Logs the exception with `LoggingService` and shows a message box. **Note:** not wired up yet, see below. | | `LoggingService` | Appends to `Logs/RPG_yyyyMMdd.log` next to the `.exe`: timestamp, message, stack trace, then the same for every inner exception. | Log entry format: ``` EXCEPTION: 29.09.2026 14:03:12 ======================================== Object reference not set to an instance of an object. at Engine.ViewModels.GameSession.set_CurrentMonster(Monster value) ... INNER EXCEPTION ---------------------------------------- ... ``` --- ## Known issues I found these by reading the code. They are listed roughly by impact, each with a suggested fix. 1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity.** [`MonsterFactory.LoadMonstersFromNodes`](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs#L69-L78) writes each monster's `` into the **same** shared `PlayerAttribute` objects and passes them to every `Monster`. [`Monster.Clone`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs#L29) then shares them again. As a result, all monsters end up with the last value loaded, the Giant Spider's 12. *Fix:* create new `PlayerAttribute` instances per monster, and copy them in `Clone()`. 2. **Possible crash when a monster kills you the moment you arrive.** If a monster wins initiative, it attacks inside the `Battle` constructor. If that attack kills the player, `OnPlayerKilled` moves them Home. That sets `CurrentMonster = null` while `_currentBattle` is still `null`, and [the setter](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs#L66-L71) dereferences it, which throws a `NullReferenceException`. The easiest way to hit this is to walk into the Spider Forest with 1–2 HP. *Fix:* start the first attack after `GameSession` has stored the battle (e.g. a separate `Battle.Start()`), and null-check `_currentBattle`. 3. **The unhandled-exception logger is never called.** `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` exists, but [`App.xaml`](WPFUI/App.xaml#L1-L6) doesn't hook it up. As a result, errors crash the app and nothing is written to `Logs/`. *Fix:* add `DispatcherUnhandledException="App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException"` to the `` element. 4. **The consumable controls are always visible.** [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L249) binds to `Inventory.HasConsumables`, but the property is called `HasConsumable`. The binding fails, so the visibility falls back to *Visible*. 5. **Overlapping rows in the player panel.** In [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L55-L85), *Experience* (row 5), *Gold* (row 6, which is clamped to row 5 because the grid has only 6 rows) and the attribute list (row 5) share one grid row and are drawn on top of each other. 6. **The Startup window has no title.** [`Startup.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/Startup.xaml#L11) binds `Title` to `GameDetails.Title`, which doesn't exist. `GameDetails.Name` was probably meant. 7. **The equipped weapon isn't restored after loading.** It is saved, but [`SaveGameService.CreatePlayer`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs#L39-L55) never reads it back. Select a weapon again after loading. 8. **T opens the trade screen even where there is no trader.** The result is an empty trade window. The hotkey should check `HasTrader` first ([MainWindow.xaml.cs](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L90)). 9. **A stale test file.** [`Test/Services/TestCombatServices`](Test/Services/TestCombatServices) has no `.cs` extension and refers to a `CombatService` class that no longer exists, so it isn't compiled. Delete it, or port it to `Battle`. 10. **`RPGState.json` is a save file from an older version.** It uses `CurrentPlayer` / `CurrentLocation` keys and cannot be loaded by the current `SaveGameService`, which expects `Player` / `XCoordinate` / `YCoordinate` in a `.rpg` file. 11. **Content typo.** The Farmer's House description mentions "Farmer **Fred**", but the trader there is "Farmer **Ted**". --- ## Limitations and ideas - Only **DEX** is used by the rules. STR could scale damage, CON could raise max HP, and CHA could affect trade prices. - **Recipes can only be learned in code** (`CharacterCreationViewModel.GetPlayer`). A recipe reward on quests or a recipe trader would open up crafting. - All three traders only stock a Pointy stick, so **crafting ingredients can't be bought** once the starting ones are used. - There is **no armour** and no defence value. Hit chance depends only on DEX. - **Levelling up doesn't heal**, and `CharacterClass` is always `"Fighter"`. - The *Help* and *About* menu items are placeholders (disabled). - **Traders aren't saved**, and they keep their state across new games in the same app session. - Windows-only: WPF plus the `xcopy` post-build step. --- ## Credits - The game's structure and starter content follow **Scott Lilly's "Build a C#/WPF RPG" tutorial series (SOSCSRPG)**. The commit history tracks progress through its lessons. - Libraries used: - [D20Tek.DiceNotation](https://github.com/d20Tek/DiceNotation) for dice rolling. - [Fody](https://github.com/Fody/Fody) / [PropertyChanged.Fody](https://github.com/Fody/PropertyChanged) for automatic `INotifyPropertyChanged`. - [Newtonsoft.Json](https://www.newtonsoft.com/json) for JSON. - [MSTest](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx) for tests.

content.text:
Written for: people opening the repo, both players and developers new to the codebase.

I've added a detailed README and a separate architecture diagram. Nothing is committed yet.

- **[docs/architecture.svg](docs/architecture.svg)** is a one-page map of the solution. It shows the five layers from the UI down to `Engine.Core`, with the main classes in each and how they call each other. It also shows how messages reach the UI, and where the game data, save files, logs and tests sit. It's shown at the top of the README and displays in both VS Code and GitHub.
- **[README.md](README.md)** covers:
  - features, and how to build, run and test the game
  - how to play: controls, screen layout and a walkthrough of the first quest
  - a world map, and the game rules with the actual combat and level-up formulas
  - tables of every item, monster, location, quest, recipe and trader
  - an architecture section with 7 more diagrams, including class diagrams, a combat step-by-step and the game loop
  - a guide to adding content, with an example "add a wolf and a new location"
  - the save-file format, a test overview, and error handling

I rendered the SVG to check its layout. All 7 diagrams in the README pass the Mermaid parser and render correctly. GitHub shows them automatically; VS Code's built-in preview needs a Mermaid extension. I also ran `dotnet build` (0 errors) and `dotnet test` (22 of 22 pass), so the commands in the README work.

**Bugs I found while reading the code.** All are in the README's "Known issues" section. The most important:
1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity (12).** `MonsterFactory` gives all monsters the same attribute objects, so the last monster loaded (Giant Spider, DEX 12) overwrites the others.
2. **Possible crash if a monster kills you the moment you arrive.** The game tries to use the fight before it has been stored, which crashes on a missing object.
3. **The error logger never runs.** The handler in `App.xaml.cs` exists but isn't connected in `App.xaml`, so errors crash the game without writing a log.
4. **Two small screen bugs:** the consumable controls are always visible because of a misspelled binding (`HasConsumables`), and Experience and Gold are drawn on top of each other in the player panel.

The Credits section names Scott Lilly's C#/WPF RPG tutorial as the source, because the game content matches it. Remove that line if you followed a different tutorial.

Want me to fix those bugs next?

lines: - [`GameItem`](Engine.Models/GameItem.cs) has a `Category` (Weapon, Consumable, Miscellanous), an `ItemTypeId`, `Name`, `Price`, `IsUnique` and an optional `IAction`. Its `Clone()` also clones the action and binds it to the new item.

- [`IAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/IAction.cs) has two implementations. [`AttackWithWeapon`](Engine.Models/Actions/AttackWithWeapon.cs) does a hit roll, then rolls damage dice. [`Heal`](Engine.Models/Actions/Heal.cs) restores HP. Both inherit [`BaseAction`](Engine.Models/Actions/BaseActions.cs), which raises `OnActionPerformed` with a human-readable result.

- [`Inventory`](Engine.Models/Inventory.cs) is immutable. `AddItem(s)` and `RemoveItem(s)` return a **new** `Inventory`. It exposes `Items`, `GroupedInventory` (for the grids), `Weapons`, `Consumables`, `HasConsumable` and `HasAllTheseItems(...)`.

-- [`Battle`](Engine.Models/Battle.cs) owns one fight. It subscribes to both combatants' events, rolls initiative, runs the attack → counter-attack exchange, hands out rewards and raises `OnCombatVictory`. It is `IDisposable` so it can unhook its event handlers.

+- [`Battle`](Engine.Models/Battle.cs) owns one fight. The constructor only subscribes to both combatants' events. `Start()` announces the monster and rolls initiative, so the monster may strike first. That happens outside the constructor so that `GameSession` already holds the battle if the first strike kills the player. file.content:
## Known issues

I found these by reading the code. They are listed roughly by impact, each with a suggested fix.

1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity.**
   [`MonsterFactory.LoadMonstersFromNodes`](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs#L69-L78) writes each monster's `<Dexterity>` into the **same** shared `PlayerAttribute` objects and passes them to every `Monster`. [`Monster.Clone`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs#L29) then shares them again. As a result, all monsters end up with the last value loaded, the Giant Spider's 12.
   *Fix:* create new `PlayerAttribute` instances per monster, and copy them in `Clone()`.

2. **Possible crash when a monster kills you the moment you arrive.**
   If a monster wins initiative, it attacks inside the `Battle` constructor. If that attack kills the player, `OnPlayerKilled` moves them Home. That sets `CurrentMonster = null` while `_currentBattle` is still `null`, and [the setter](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs#L66-L71) dereferences it, which throws a `NullReferenceException`. The easiest way to hit this is to walk into the Spider Forest with 1–2 HP.
   *Fix:* start the first attack after `GameSession` has stored the battle (e.g. a separate `Battle.Start()`), and null-check `_currentBattle`.

3. **The unhandled-exception logger is never called.**
   `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` exists, but [`App.xaml`](WPFUI/App.xaml#L1-L6) doesn't hook it up. As a result, errors crash the app and nothing is written to `Logs/`.
   *Fix:* add `DispatcherUnhandledException="App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException"` to the `<Application>` element.

4. **The consumable controls are always visible.**
   [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L249) binds to `Inventory.HasConsumables`, but the property is called `HasConsumable`. The binding fails, so the visibility falls back to *Visible*.

5. **Overlapping rows in the player panel.**
   In [`MainWindow.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml#L55-L85), *Experience* (row 5), *Gold* (row 6, which is clamped to row 5 because the grid has only 6 rows) and the attribute list (row 5) share one grid row and are drawn on top of each other.

6. **The Startup window has no title.** [`Startup.xaml`](WPFUI/Windows/Startup.xaml#L11) binds `Title` to `GameDetails.Title`, which doesn't exist. `GameDetails.Name` was probably meant.

7. **The equipped weapon isn't restored after loading.** It is saved, but [`SaveGameService.CreatePlayer`](Engine.Services/SaveGameService.cs#L39-L55) never reads it back. Select a weapon again after loading.

8. **<kbd>T</kbd> opens the trade screen even where there is no trader.** The result is an empty trade window. The hotkey should check `HasTrader` first ([MainWindow.xaml.cs](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L90)).

9. **A stale test file.** [`Test/Services/TestCombatServices`](Test/Services/TestCombatServices) has no `.cs` extension and refers to a `CombatService` class that no longer exists, so it isn't compiled. Delete it, or port it to `Battle`.

10. **`RPGState.json` is a save file from an older version.** It uses `CurrentPlayer` / `CurrentLocation` keys and cannot be loaded by the current `SaveGameService`, which expects `Player` / `XCoordinate` / `YCoordinate` in a `.rpg` file.

11. **Content typo.** The Farmer's House description mentions "Farmer **Fred**", but the trader there is "Farmer **Ted**".

---

I found these by reading the code. They are listed roughly by impact, each with a suggested fix.

1. **Every monster fights with the same Dexterity.**
   [`MonsterFactory.LoadMonstersFromNodes`](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs#L69-L78) writes each monster's `<Dexterity>` into the **same** shared `PlayerAttribute` objects and passes them to every `Monster`. [`Monster.Clone`](Engine.Models/Monster.cs#L29) then shares them again. As a result, all monsters end up with the last value loaded, the Giant Spider's 12.
   *Fix:* create new `PlayerAttribute` instances per monster, and copy them in `Clone()`.

2. **Possible crash when a monster kills you the moment you arrive.**
   If a monster wins initiative, it attacks inside the `Battle` constructor. If that attack kills the player, `OnPlayerKilled` moves them Home. That sets `CurrentMonster = null` while `_currentBattle` is still `null`, and [the setter](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs#L66-L71) dereferences it, which throws a `NullReferenceException`. The easiest way to hit this is to walk into the Spider Forest with 1–2 HP.
   *Fix:* start the first attack after `GameSession` has stored the battle (e.g. a separate `Battle.Start()`), and null-check `_currentBattle`.

3. **The unhandled-exception logger is never called.**
   `App_OnDispatcherUnhandledException` exists, but [`App.xaml`](WPFUI/App.xaml#L1-L6) doesn't hook it up. As a result, errors crash the app and nothing is written to `Logs/`.

content.text:
I fixed all four bugs, and a new test or before-and-after screenshot confirms each one. Nothing is committed.

| Bug | Fix | How I checked it |
|---|---|---|
| Every monster fought with the Giant Spider's DEX of 12 | Each monster now gets its own copy of its attributes when it's loaded and every time it spawns. I added a `Clone()` to [PlayerAttribute.cs](Engine.Models/PlayerAttribute.cs) and use it in [MonsterFactory.cs](Engine.Services/Factories/MonsterFactory.cs) and [Monster.cs](Engine.Models/Monster.cs). | New tests failed before the fix (Snake had DEX 12 instead of 15) and pass now. |
| Crash when a monster killed you the moment you arrived | The monster's first strike moved from the `Battle` constructor into a new `Battle.Start()` in [Battle.cs](Engine.Models/Battle.cs). [GameSession.cs](Engine.ViewModels/GameSession.cs) calls it only after storing the battle, so dying on arrival sends you Home cleanly. | A new test crashed with a `NullReferenceException` before the fix. It passes now, and it passed 8 more runs in a row. |
| Error logger never ran | Connected the existing handler in [App.xaml](WPFUI/App.xaml). The game still closes after showing the error, but it now writes the log file first. | The solution builds, which checks that the handler exists. |
| Consumable box always shown; *Experience* and *Gold* missing from the player panel | Corrected the misspelled `HasConsumable` binding and gave each stat its own row in [MainWindow.xaml](WPFUI/Windows/MainWindow.xaml). | Screenshots of the real window before and after: *Experience* and *Gold* now appear, and the consumable box hides when you carry none. |

The build has 0 errors, and all 25 tests pass (the 22 existing ones plus 3 new). I also updated the README and the diagram: the fixed bugs are gone from Known issues, and the test counts and combat description match the new code.

**New issue found while checking:** messages raised while a game is starting never reach the message log. In the screenshot, a Snake hit the player on arrival but the log stayed empty. This is because `MainWindow` subscribes to messages only after it creates the game session. I added it to Known issues instead of fixing it here.

**Git housekeeping:** `Test/obj/` is still tracked by git, so every build changes those files. `git rm -r --cached Test/obj` would stop that.
